title.en: Volume 85 Biographies 35: Tang Lin, Zhang Wenguan, Xu Yougong
title.raw: 卷八十五 列傳第三十五: 唐臨 張文瓘 徐有功 Volume 85 Biographies 35: Tang Lin, Zhang Wenguan, Xu Yougong

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑字懷英，并州太原人也。

translations.literal: Di Renjie—Di Renjie, styled Huaiying, was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie, whose courtesy name was Huaiying, came from Taiyuan in Bing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖孝緒，貞觀中尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiaoxu was Left Vice Director of the Secretariat in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Di Xiaoxu had served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat under Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 父知遜，夔州長史。

translations.literal: His father Zhixun was Regional Commander of Kui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Di Zhixun had been prefectural secretary in Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 仁傑兒童時，門人有被害者，縣吏就詰之，眾皆接對，唯仁傑堅坐讀書。

translations.literal: When Renjie was a child, a retainer in the household was murdered; county clerks came to question them. Everyone answered the interrogation; only Renjie sat firmly reading his books.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, when a household retainer was killed and county officers came to question everyone, they all responded while Renjie alone remained seated, reading.

sentences.zh: 吏責之，仁傑曰：「黃卷之中，聖賢備在，猶不能接對，何暇偶俗吏，而見責耶！」

translations.literal: The clerk reproved him. Renjie said: "Within the yellow scrolls the sages and worthies are fully present; I still could not respond to questioning—how would I have leisure to converse with vulgar clerks, only to be reproved?
translations.idiomatic: When an officer scolded him, Renjie replied: "The sages are all there in my books, and I still could not face your questioning—what leisure would I have to bandy words with a petty clerk and earn rebuke for it?"

sentences.zh: 後以明經舉，授汴州判佐。

translations.literal: Later, having passed the Mingjing examination, he was appointed assistant administrator of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later passed the Classics examination and was appointed adjutant in Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時工部尚書閻立本爲河南道黜陟使，仁傑爲吏人誣告，立本見而謝曰：「仲尼云：『觀過知仁矣。』

translations.literal: At the time the Minister of Works Yan Liben was promotion-and-demotion commissioner for the Henan circuit. Renjie was falsely accused by clerks. Liben saw him and apologized, saying: "Confucius said: 'By observing his faults one may know his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Liben, Minister of Works, was touring Henan as promotion-and-demotion commissioner, clerks falsely accused Renjie. Liben met him and apologized, quoting Confucius: "One may know a man's benevolence from his faults.

sentences.zh: 足下可謂海曲之明珠，東南之遺寶。」

translations.literal: You may be called a bright pearl of the sea's bend, a lost treasure of the southeast.'
translations.idiomatic: You are a pearl from the coast, a treasure the southeast had overlooked."

sentences.zh: 薦授并州都督府法曹。

translations.literal: He recommended him and appointed him legal officer of the Bingzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Renjie for appointment as legal officer in the Bingzhou metropolitan government.

sentences.zh: 其親在河陽別業，仁傑赴并州，登太行山，南望見白雲孤飛，謂左右曰：「吾親所居，在此雲下。」

translations.literal: His parents were at a separate estate in Heyang. Renjie was traveling to Bingzhou and climbed Mount Taihang. Looking south he saw a lone white cloud drifting and said to those beside him: "Where my parents dwell lies beneath this cloud.
translations.idiomatic: His parents lived at a family estate in Heyang. On his way to Bingzhou he climbed the Taihang range, and gazing south at a solitary white cloud, he told his attendants: "My parents' home lies beneath that cloud."

sentences.zh: 瞻望佇立久之，雲移乃行。

translations.literal: He gazed and stood a long while; only when the cloud moved did he proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He stood watching for a long time and did not move on until the cloud had drifted away.

sentences.zh: 仁傑孝友絶人，在并州，有同府法曹鄭崇質，母老且病，當充使絶域。

translations.literal: Renjie's filial piety and brotherly affection surpassed others. While in Bingzhou there was a fellow legal officer in the prefecture, Zheng Chongzhi, whose mother was old and ill and who was due to serve as envoy to a distant region.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie's devotion to parents and kin was extraordinary. In Bingzhou a colleague in the legal bureau, Zheng Chongzhi, had an aged, ailing mother yet was assigned to go as envoy to a far frontier.

sentences.zh: 仁傑謂曰：「太夫人有危疾，而公遠使，豈可貽親萬里之憂！」

translations.literal: Renjie said to him: "Your lady mother has a grave illness, yet you are to go on a distant mission—how could you leave your parent the worry of a thousand li?
translations.idiomatic: Renjie told him: "Your mother is gravely ill, and you are to travel thousands of miles—how can you lay that burden on her?"

sentences.zh: 乃詣長史藺仁基，請代崇質而行。

translations.literal: He then went to Chief Administrator Lan Renji and asked to go in Chongzhi's place.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Chief Administrator Lan Renji and volunteered to take Chongzhi's place on the mission.

sentences.zh: 時仁基與司馬李孝廉不協，因謂曰：「吾等豈獨無愧耶？」

translations.literal: At the time Renji was not on good terms with Vice Prefect Li Xiaolian, and therefore said to him: "Are we alone without shame?
translations.idiomatic: Renji had been at odds with Vice Prefect Li Xiaolian; he now said to him: "Should we not be ashamed as well?"

sentences.zh: 由是相待如初。

translations.literal: From this they treated each other as at first.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the two men were reconciled.

sentences.zh: 仁傑，儀鳳中爲大理丞，周歳斷滯獄一萬七千人，無冤訴者。

translations.literal: Renjie, in the Yifeng era served as assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review; within a year he decided seventeen thousand backlog cases, and none complained of injustice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng period Renjie served as assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and within a year cleared seventeen thousand pending cases, with no one left protesting wrongful judgment.

sentences.zh: 時武衞大將軍權善才坐誤斫昭陵柏樹，仁傑奏罪當免職。

translations.literal: At the time General of the Martial Guard Regiment Quan Shancai was charged with mistakenly cutting a cypress at Zhaoling. Renjie memorialized that the crime warranted dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: When General Quan Shancai of the Martial Guard was charged with accidentally felling a cypress at Emperor Taizong's mausoleum, Renjie argued the offense merited only removal from office.

sentences.zh: 高宗令即誅之，仁傑又奏罪不當死。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong ordered him executed at once. Renjie again memorialized that the crime did not warrant death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong ordered immediate execution, but Renjie submitted again that the crime did not deserve death.

sentences.zh: 帝作色曰：「善才斫陵上樹，是使我不孝，必須殺之。」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said: "Shancai cut a tree on the mausoleum—this makes me unfilial; he must be killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed with anger and said: "By cutting a tree on the imperial tomb Shancai has made me fail in filial duty—I must have him killed."

sentences.zh: 左右矚仁傑令出，仁傑曰：「臣聞逆龍鱗，忤人主，自古以爲難，臣愚以爲不然。

translations.literal: Those at his side signaled Renjie to withdraw. Renjie said: "I have heard that to go against the dragon's scales and offend one's lord has from antiquity been thought difficult; this foolish subject does not think so.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants signaled Renjie to withdraw, but he said: "They say it is hard to touch the dragon's scales and oppose one's sovereign—I do not believe it.

sentences.zh: 居桀、紂時則難，堯、舜時則易。

translations.literal: Under Jie and Zhou it was difficult; under Yao and Shun it was easy.
translations.idiomatic: Under tyrants like Jie and Zhou it was hard; under rulers like Yao and Shun it was easy.

sentences.zh: 臣今幸逢堯、舜，不懼比干之誅。

translations.literal: Your subject now fortunately meets Yao and Shun and does not fear execution like Bigan.
translations.idiomatic: I am fortunate to serve a Yao or a Shun and need not fear dying like Bigan.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文時有盜高廟玉環，張釋之廷諍，罪止棄市。

translations.literal: Formerly in the time of Emperor Wen of Han someone stole a jade ring from the Gaozu temple; Zhang Shizhi remonstrated at court, and the punishment stopped at public execution in the market.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Wendi's reign, when thieves stole a jade ring from the founder's temple, Zhang Shizhi argued in open court and limited the penalty to execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 魏文將徙其人，辛毗引裾而諫，亦見納用。

translations.literal: When King Wen of Wei was about to relocate his people, Xin Pi seized his robe and remonstrated, and this too was accepted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wen of Wei planned to move his people, Xin Pi seized his robe to protest, and his counsel was heeded.

sentences.zh: 且明主可以理奪，忠臣不可以威懼。

translations.literal: Moreover, an enlightened lord may be swayed by reason; a loyal minister cannot be cowed by intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler yields to reason; a loyal minister is not frightened by threats.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不納臣言，瞑目之後，羞見釋之、辛毗於地下。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty now does not accept your subject's words, after I close my eyes I shall be ashamed to meet Shizhi and Xin Pi in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not heed me, when I am dead I shall be ashamed to face Zhang Shizhi and Xin Pi below.

sentences.zh: 陛下作法，懸之象魏，徒流死罪，俱有等差。

translations.literal: Your Majesty makes laws and hangs them at the symbolic gate; exile, banishment, and death all have their gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has promulgated laws and posted them at the gate; exile, penal servitude, and death each have their proper degree.

sentences.zh: 豈有犯非極刑，即令賜死？

translations.literal: How can there be an offense that is not the extreme penalty yet an order to grant death?
translations.idiomatic: How can a crime that is not capital be punished with immediate execution?

sentences.zh: 法既無常，則萬姓何所措其手足？

translations.literal: If the law is without constancy, where shall the myriad people place their hands and feet?
translations.idiomatic: If the law has no fixed measure, how are the people to know what to do?

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲變法，請從今日爲始。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must change the law, please let it begin from today.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on changing the law, let the change begin today.

sentences.zh: 古人云：『假使盜長陵一抔土，陛下何以加之？』

translations.literal: The ancients said: "Suppose someone stole a handful of earth from Changling—how would Your Majesty punish him?"
translations.idiomatic: The ancients asked: if someone stole a handful of soil from the founder's tomb, what penalty would Your Majesty impose?

sentences.zh: 今陛下以昭陵一株柏殺一將軍，千載之後，謂陛下爲何主？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, for one cypress at Zhaoling, would kill a general. A thousand years hence, what sort of ruler will men call Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, for one cypress at Zhaoling, you would kill a general—what will posterity call such a ruler?

sentences.zh: 此臣所以不敢奉制殺善才，陷陛下於不道。」

translations.literal: This is why your subject dares not follow the order to kill Shancai and involve Your Majesty in unrighteous conduct."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I dare not obey an order to kill Shancai and make Your Majesty guilty of injustice."

sentences.zh: 帝意稍解，善才因而免死。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind gradually eased, and Shancai thereby escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger subsided, and Shancai was spared.

sentences.zh: 居數日，授仁傑侍御史。

translations.literal: Within several days Renjie was appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Renjie was appointed attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 時司農卿韋機兼領將作、少府二司，高宗以恭陵玄宮狹小，不容送終之具，遣機續成其功。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Agriculture Wei Ji concurrently headed the Directorate of Palace Buildings and the Court of the Imperial Treasury. Emperor Gaozong, because the underground chamber of Gongling was narrow and could not hold the funerary furnishings, sent Ji to complete the work.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji, Minister of Agriculture, also headed the offices of palace construction and the imperial workshops. Because the burial chamber at Gongling was too small for the funeral furnishings, Gaozong had him enlarge it.

sentences.zh: 機於埏之左右爲便房四所，又造宿羽、高山、上陽等宮，莫不壯麗。

translations.literal: Ji built four convenient chambers on either side of the mound, and also constructed the Suyu, Gaoshan, Shangyang, and other palaces, all of them grand and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: He built four side chambers around the tomb mound and also erected the Suyu, Gaoshan, Shangyang, and other palaces, each magnificent.

sentences.zh: 仁傑奏其太過，機竟坐免官。

translations.literal: Renjie memorialized that this was excessive; Ji in the end was punished by dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie protested the extravagance, and Wei Ji was eventually dismissed.

sentences.zh: 左司郎中王本立恃寵用事，朝廷懾懼，仁傑奏之，請付法寺，高宗特原之。

translations.literal: Left Bureau Director Wang Benli relied on favor to wield power; the court was fearful. Renjie memorialized against him and asked that he be handed to the judicial office. Emperor Gaozong specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Benli of the Left Bureau abused imperial favor and terrified the court. Renjie impeached him and asked that he be tried, but Gaozong personally pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 仁傑奏曰：「國家雖乏英才，豈少本立之類，陛下何惜罪人而虧王法？

translations.literal: Renjie memorialized: "Although the state lacks outstanding talent, are men like Benli so few? Why should Your Majesty spare a criminal and impair the royal law?
translations.idiomatic: Renjie argued: "The empire may lack talent, but men like Benli are not rare—why spare a guilty man and damage the law?

sentences.zh: 必欲曲赦本立，請棄臣於無人之境，爲忠貞將來之誡。」

translations.literal: If you must bend the law to pardon Benli, please abandon your subject in a place where no man dwells, as a warning to the loyal and steadfast in times to come.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty must pardon Benli, cast me out to some desolate place as a warning to loyal men hereafter."

sentences.zh: 本立竟得罪，由是朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: Benli in the end was punished; from this the court became solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Benli was punished after all, and the court grew orderly.

sentences.zh: 尋加朝散大夫，累遷度支郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure and was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Master of Palace Leisure and rose to director of the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 高宗將幸汾陽宮，以仁傑爲知頓使。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong was about to visit Fenyang Palace and appointed Renjie commissioner for provisioning halts.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Run whispered to Liu Kun, "Linghu Sheng means to urge you, my lord, to claim the throne."

sentences.zh: 并州長史李沖玄以道出妒女祠，俗云盛服過者必致風雷之災，乃發數萬人別開御道。

translations.literal: Bingzhou Chief Administrator Li Chongxuan, because the road passed the Jealous Woman Shrine and common lore said that those in splendid dress who passed would bring wind and thunder disasters, mobilized tens of thousands of men to open a separate imperial road.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongxuan, chief administrator of Bingzhou, feared the route passed the Jealous Woman Shrine, where local belief held that richly dressed travelers would stir storms; he drafted tens of thousands of laborers to build a new imperial road.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「天子之行，千乘萬騎，風伯清塵，雨師灑道，何妒女之害耶？」

translations.literal: Renjie said: "When the Son of Heaven travels, a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen go with him; the Wind Lord clears the dust and the Rain Master sprinkles the road—what harm from a jealous woman?
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said: "When the Son of Heaven travels, he has thousands of chariots and horsemen—the Wind Lord clears the dust and the Rain Master wets the road. What harm can a jealous woman's shrine do?"

sentences.zh: 遽令罷之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the project halted at once.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞之，歎曰：「真大丈夫也！」

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong heard of it he sighed and said: "A true great man!"
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong heard of this he exclaimed: "A true man!"

sentences.zh: 俄轉寧州刺史，撫和戎夏，人得歡心，郡人勒碑頌德。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Prefect of Ningzhou, where he soothed and harmonized the barbarians and Chinese; the people found joy in him, and the commandery erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Ningzhou, where he reconciled Chinese and non-Chinese subjects alike; the people loved him, and the prefecture set up a stele in his praise.

sentences.zh: 御史郭翰巡察隴右，所至多所按劾。

translations.literal: Censor Guo Han inspected Longyou; wherever he arrived he impeached many.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Guo Han toured Longyou he impeached officials wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 及入寧州境內，耆老歌刺史德美者盈路。

translations.literal: When he entered the territory of Ningzhou, elders singing of the prefect's beautiful virtue filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Ningzhou he found the roads lined with elders singing the prefect's praises.

sentences.zh: 翰既授館，召州吏謂之曰：「入其境，其政可知也。

translations.literal: After Han had been lodged, he summoned the prefectural clerks and said to them: "Having entered its borders, its governance is already known.
translations.idiomatic: After taking lodging he summoned the prefectural staff and said: "One can tell the quality of rule the moment one crosses the border.

sentences.zh: 願成使君之美，無爲久留。」

translations.literal: I wish to complete the lord's excellence and not stay long.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather add to the prefect's reputation than linger here."

sentences.zh: 州人方散。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 翰薦名於朝，徵爲冬官侍郎，充江南巡撫使。

translations.literal: Han recommended his name to the court; he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Public Works and appointed Jiangnan touring commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Han recommended him to the court; Renjie was summoned as vice minister of public works and made touring commissioner of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 吳、楚之俗多淫祠，仁傑奏毀一千七百所，唯留夏禹、吳太伯、季劄、伍員四祠。

translations.literal: The customs of Wu and Chu had many licentious shrines. Renjie memorialized the destruction of seventeen hundred, keeping only the shrines of Yu of Xia, Taibo of Wu, Jizha, and Wu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Chu were rife with improper shrines; Renjie had seventeen hundred demolished, sparing only those of Yu the Great, Taibo of Wu, Jizha, and Wu Zixu.

sentences.zh: 轉文昌右丞，出爲豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and went out as Prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice director of the Secretariat and sent out as prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時越王貞稱兵汝南事敗，緣坐者六七百人，籍沒者五千口，司刑使逼促行刑。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Yue of the Yue lineage raised troops in Runan and failed; those implicated numbered six or seven hundred, and five thousand persons were registered for confiscation. The judicial commissioner pressed for speedy execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yue rebelled in Runan and was defeated, six or seven hundred people were implicated and five thousand more faced confiscation of property; the judicial commissioner pressed for executions.

sentences.zh: 仁傑哀其詿誤，緩其獄，密表奏曰：「臣欲顯奏，似爲逆人申理；

translations.literal: Renjie pitied their entanglement in error, slowed the cases, and secretly memorialized: "Your subject wishes to memorialize openly, yet it would seem to plead the case for rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Renjie pitied those caught up in the affair, slowed the trials, and sent a secret memorial: "If I speak openly I may seem to plead for rebels;

sentences.zh: 知而不言，恐乖陛下存恤之旨。

translations.literal: yet knowing and not speaking, I fear I would violate Your Majesty's intent to preserve and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: yet if I know and stay silent I fear I betray Your Majesty's merciful intent.

sentences.zh: 表成復毀，意不能定。

translations.literal: When the memorial was finished he destroyed it again; his mind could not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the memorial, destroyed it, and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 此輩鹹非本心，伏望哀其詿誤。」

translations.literal: These people are all not of rebellious heart in themselves; I humbly hope you will pity their entanglement in error.
translations.idiomatic: These people did not rebel of their own will; I beg Your Majesty to pity their mistake."

sentences.zh: 特敕原之，配流豐州。

translations.literal: A special edict pardoned them; they were assigned to exile in Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially pardoned them and sent them into exile at Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 豫囚次於寧州，父老迎而勞之曰：「我狄使君活汝輩耶！」

translations.literal: The Yuzhou prisoners stopped at Ningzhou; the elders came out to welcome and comfort them, saying: "Did our Lord Di save you all?
translations.idiomatic: As the prisoners from Yuzhou passed through Ningzhou, the elders came out to greet them: "Did our Commissioner Di save you?"

sentences.zh: 相攜哭於碑下，齋三日而後行。

translations.literal: They supported one another weeping beneath the stele, observed fasting for three days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together at the stele, fasted three days, and then went on.

sentences.zh: 豫囚至流所，復相與立碑頌狄君之德。

translations.literal: When the Yuzhou prisoners reached the place of exile, they again together erected a stele praising Lord Di's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At their place of exile the Yuzhou prisoners again joined in erecting a stele praising Commissioner Di.

sentences.zh: 初，越王之亂，宰相張光輔率師討平之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the rebellion of the Prince of Yue, Chancellor Zhang Guangfu led troops to suppress and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yue rebelled, Chancellor Zhang Guangfu led the army that suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 將士恃功，多所求取，仁傑不之應。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers relied on their merit and made many demands; Renjie did not respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: His officers, flush with victory, made many demands, which Renjie refused.

sentences.zh: 光輔怒曰：「州將輕元帥耶？」

translations.literal: Guangfu angrily said: "Does the prefect slight the commander-in-chief?
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu snapped: "Does the prefect hold the commander in contempt?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「亂河南者，一越王貞耳。

translations.literal: Renjie said: "He who disturbed Henan was only one man, Prince Yue Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie replied: "Only one man disturbed Henan—Prince Yue.

sentences.zh: 今一貞死而萬貞生。」

translations.literal: Now one Zhen dies and ten thousand Zhen are born."
translations.idiomatic: Now one Yue is dead, but ten thousand Yues are being born."

sentences.zh: 光輔質其辭，仁傑曰：「明公董戎三十萬，平一亂臣，不戢兵鋒，縱其暴橫，無罪之人，肝腦塗地，此非萬貞何耶？

translations.literal: Guangfu questioned his words. Renjie said: "My lord directed three hundred thousand troops, pacified one rebellious minister, yet did not sheath the weapons' edge and let them run rampant; innocent people had their livers and brains smeared on the ground—is this not ten thousand Zhen?
translations.idiomatic: When Guangfu challenged him, Renjie said: "You led three hundred thousand men to crush one rebel, yet failed to restrain your troops. Innocent people were slaughtered—is that not breeding ten thousand Yues?

sentences.zh: 且凶威協從，勢難自固，及天兵暫臨，乘城歸順者萬計，繩墜四面成蹊。

translations.literal: Moreover, when fierce intimidation coerced followers, their position could hardly hold firm; when the imperial army briefly arrived, those who mounted the walls to submit numbered in the tens of thousands, and ropes let down on all four sides made paths.
translations.idiomatic: Men joined the rebels only under coercion; when imperial troops arrived, tens of thousands climbed the walls to surrender, and ropes hung on every side like paths.

sentences.zh: 公奈何縱邀功之人，殺歸降之眾？

translations.literal: Why should my lord indulge those who seek merit and kill the masses who had returned in submission?
translations.idiomatic: Why let men hungry for credit kill those who had already submitted?

sentences.zh: 但恐冤聲騰沸，上徹於天。

translations.literal: I only fear that cries of injustice will boil up and reach heaven above.
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that the outcry of the wronged will rise to heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 如得尚方斬馬劍加於君頸，雖死如歸。」

translations.literal: If I could have the imperial execution sword placed on my lord's neck, I would die content."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the imperial sword were laid to your neck, I would die content."

sentences.zh: 光輔不能詰，心甚銜之。

translations.literal: Guangfu could not rebut him and bore a deep grudge in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu had no answer and nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 還都，奏仁傑不遜，左授復州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he memorialized that Renjie was insubordinate; Renjie was demoted by one rank to Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he accused Renjie of insubordination, and Renjie was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 入爲洛州司馬。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as vice prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 天授二年九月丁酉，轉地官侍郎、判尚書、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the ninth month of the second year of Tianshou he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, acting Director of the Secretariat, and Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace with the rank of Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the ninth month of Tianshou 2 (691), he became vice minister of revenue, acting director of the secretariat, and associate grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 則天謂曰：「卿在汝南時，甚有善政，欲知譖卿者乎？」

translations.literal: Empress Wu Zetian said to him: "When you were in Runan you had very good governance. Do you wish to know who slandered you?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said: "You governed Runan well. Would you like to know who denounced you?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑謝曰：「陛下以臣爲過，臣當改之；

translations.literal: Renjie declined and said: "If Your Majesty holds that your subject has faults, your subject should reform them;
translations.idiomatic: Renjie replied: "If Your Majesty finds fault in me, I shall reform;

sentences.zh: 陛下明臣無過，臣之幸也。

translations.literal: if Your Majesty understands that your subject has no faults, that is your subject's good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty knows I am without fault, that is my good fortune.

sentences.zh: 臣不知譖者，並爲善友，臣請不知。」

translations.literal: Your subject does not wish to know the slanderers; let them all be good friends. Your subject asks not to know."
translations.idiomatic: I do not wish to know my accusers—let them remain my friends. I beg to remain ignorant."

sentences.zh: 則天深加歎異。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The empress marveled at this.

sentences.zh: 未幾，爲來俊臣誣構下獄。

translations.literal: Before long he was framed by Lai Junchen and cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lai Junchen framed him and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 時一問即承者例得減死，來俊臣逼協仁傑，令一問承反。

translations.literal: At the time those who confessed upon a single interrogation were by precedent granted commuted death. Lai Junchen coerced Renjie and ordered him to confess rebellion upon one questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Confessing at the first interrogation could reduce a capital sentence; Lai Junchen pressured Renjie to admit treason immediately.

sentences.zh: 仁傑歎曰：「大周革命，萬物唯新，唐朝舊臣，甘從誅戮。

translations.literal: Renjie sighed and said: "The Great Zhou has transformed the realm; all things are renewed. An old minister of Tang willingly accepts execution.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie sighed: "The Zhou has renewed all things; as an old servant of Tang I accept execution.

sentences.zh: 反是實！」

translations.literal: Rebellion is the truth!
translations.idiomatic: Treason it is, then!"

sentences.zh: 俊臣乃少寬之。

translations.literal: Junchen then relaxed the pressure somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen then eased his pressure.

sentences.zh: 判官王德壽謂仁傑曰：「尚書必得減死。

translations.literal: Judge Wang Deshou said to Renjie: "The Director will certainly obtain commuted death.
translations.idiomatic: The examining judge Wang Deshou told Renjie: "You will surely receive a reduced sentence.

sentences.zh: 德壽意欲求少階級，憑尚書牽楊執柔，可乎？」

translations.literal: Deshou's intent is to seek a small promotion in rank. Might I rely on the Director to implicate Yang Zhirou—would that be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Deshou said he wanted a small promotion—would Renjie implicate Yang Zhirou for him?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「若何牽之？」

translations.literal: Renjie said: "How would one implicate him?"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie asked: "How would I implicate him?"

sentences.zh: 德壽曰：「尚書爲春官時，執柔任其司員外，引之可也。」

translations.literal: Deshou said: "When the Director was in the Ministry of Personnel, Zhirou served as his bureau assistant outside the regular roster; you could implicate him."
translations.idiomatic: Deshou said: "When you were in the Ministry of Personnel, Zhirou was your bureau aide—you could name him."

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「皇天后土，遣仁傑行此事！」

translations.literal: Renjie said: "Heaven and Earth—would they send Renjie to do such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie cried: "Heaven and Earth—would they have me do such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 以頭觸柱，流血被面，德壽懼而謝焉。

translations.literal: He struck his head against a pillar; blood covered his face. Deshou was afraid and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: He dashed his head against a pillar until blood covered his face; Deshou fled in terror and apologized.

sentences.zh: 既承反，所司但待日行刑，不復嚴備。

translations.literal: Once rebellion had been confessed, the office concerned only awaited the day of execution and no longer kept strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had confessed, the authorities merely waited for execution day and relaxed their watch.

sentences.zh: 仁傑求守者得筆硯，拆被頭帛書冤，置綿衣中，謂德壽曰：「時方熱，請付家人去其綿。」

translations.literal: Renjie asked the guard and obtained brush and inkstone, tore open the cotton at the head of his quilt, wrote of his injustice, placed it in his padded garment, and said to Deshou: "The season is hot; please give this to my family to remove the padding."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie persuaded a guard to lend him brush and ink, tore open his quilt lining to write his plea of innocence, hid the note in his padded coat, and told Deshou: "It is hot—please send this to my family to remove the padding."

sentences.zh: 德壽不之察。

translations.literal: Deshou did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Deshou noticed nothing amiss.

sentences.zh: 仁傑子光遠得書，持以告變。

translations.literal: Renjie's son Guangyuan obtained the letter and took it to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie's son Guangyuan retrieved the letter and brought it forward as a complaint.

sentences.zh: 則天召見，覽之而問俊臣。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian summoned him for audience, read it, and questioned Junchen.
translations.idiomatic: The empress summoned Guangyuan, read the letter, and questioned Lai Junchen.

sentences.zh: 俊臣曰：「仁傑不免冠帶，寢處甚安，何由伏罪？」

translations.literal: Junchen said: "Renjie has not removed cap and sash; his sleeping quarters are quite comfortable—how could he confess guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen said: "Renjie still wears his cap and sash and sleeps in comfort—how could he have confessed?"

sentences.zh: 則天使人視之，俊臣遽命仁傑巾帶而見使者。

translations.literal: The empress sent someone to look; Junchen hurriedly ordered Renjie to put on cap and sash and appear before the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The empress sent an inspector; Lai Junchen at once had Renjie dress in cap and sash to meet him.

sentences.zh: 乃令德壽代仁傑作謝死表，附使者進之。

translations.literal: He then had Deshou draft a death-petition of thanks on Renjie's behalf and had the envoy submit it.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Deshou write a memorial of thanks for execution in Renjie's name and sent it in with the envoy.

sentences.zh: 則天召仁傑，謂曰：「承反何也？」

translations.literal: Wu Zetian summoned Renjie and said: "Why did you confess rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian summoned Renjie and asked: "Why did you confess treason?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「向若不承反，已死於鞭笞矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Had I not confessed rebellion earlier, I would already have died under the lash."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "If I had not confessed, I would already be dead from the beating."

sentences.zh: 「何爲作謝死表？」

translations.literal: Why did you write a death-petition of thanks?"
translations.idiomatic: "Then why was there a memorial thanking you for execution?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣無此表。」

translations.literal: He said: "Your subject has no such memorial."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "I wrote no such memorial."

sentences.zh: 示之，乃知代署也。

translations.literal: They showed it to him; then he knew it had been signed in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When they showed it to him, he saw it had been forged in his name.

sentences.zh: 故得免死。

translations.literal: Thus he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 貶彭澤令。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Magistrate of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to magistrate of Pengze.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣屢奏請誅之，則天曰：「朕好生惡殺，誌在恤刑。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi repeatedly memorialized requesting his execution. Wu Zetian said: "I love life and hate killing; my purpose is to show compassion in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi repeatedly asked that he be put to death, but Wu Zetian said: "I love life and abhor killing; my aim is mercy in punishment.

sentences.zh: 渙汗已行，不可更返。」

translations.literal: The decree of mercy has already been issued; it cannot be reversed."
translations.idiomatic: The pardon has already gone forth and cannot be withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 萬歳通天年，契丹寇陷冀州，河北震動，征仁傑爲魏州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Wansuitongtian era, the Khitan raided and captured Jizhou; Hebei was shaken; Renjie was summoned as Prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansuitongtian reign period the Khitan attacked and took Jizhou, throwing Hebei into alarm; Renjie was appointed prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 前刺史獨孤思莊懼賊至，盡驅百姓入城，繕修守具。

translations.literal: The former prefect Dugu Sizhuang, fearing the bandits' arrival, drove all the people into the city and repaired defense equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect, Dugu Sizhuang, fearing an attack, herded every civilian into the city and rushed to repair its defenses.

sentences.zh: 仁傑既至，悉放歸農畝，謂曰：「賊猶在遠，何必如是。

translations.literal: When Renjie arrived, he released them all back to their fields and said: "The bandits are still far away—why do this?
translations.idiomatic: When Renjie arrived he sent them all back to their farms, saying: "The enemy is still far off—why go to such extremes?

sentences.zh: 萬一賊來，吾自當之，必不關百姓也。」

translations.literal: If by chance bandits come, I myself will meet them—it will surely not involve the common people.
translations.idiomatic: If they do come, I will face them myself—the people will not be dragged into it."

sentences.zh: 賊聞之自退，百姓咸歌誦之，相與立碑以紀恩惠。

translations.literal: When the bandits heard this they withdrew of themselves; the people all sang and praised him, and together erected a stele to record his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders withdrew on hearing this; the people sang his praises and together raised a stele to commemorate his kindness.

sentences.zh: 俄轉幽州都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Area Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to area commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 神功元年，入爲鸞臺侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，加銀青光祿大夫，兼納言。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shendong he entered court as Vice Director of the Luantai, Joint Same-Fengge-Luantai Grand Counselor, promoted to Silver-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and concurrently Director of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In 697 he entered court as vice director of the Censorate and co–grand counselor of the Fengge and Luantai, promoted to Silver-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and made director of edicts as well.

sentences.zh: 仁傑以百姓西戍疏勒等四鎮，極爲凋弊，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Renjie, seeing that the people suffered extreme hardship from garrison duty in the west at Kucha and the other Four Garrisons, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how badly the people were exhausted by western garrison duty at Kucha and the other Four Garrisons, Renjie submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天生四夷，皆在先王封疆之外。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Heaven gave birth to the Four Yi, all lying beyond the frontiers established by the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Heaven created the four barbarian quarters, all beyond the borders set by the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 故東拒滄海，西隔流沙，北橫大漠，南阻五嶺，此天所以限夷狄而隔中外也。

translations.literal: Thus the east is bounded by the dark sea, the west separated by drifting sands, the north crossed by the great desert, the south blocked by the Five Ridges—this is how Heaven confines the Yi and Di and separates inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: The east is bounded by the sea, the west by drifting sands, the north by the great desert, and the south by the Five Ridges—Heaven's way of confining the barbarians and separating them from the heartland.

sentences.zh: 自典籍所紀，聲教所及，三代不能至者，國家盡兼之矣。

translations.literal: From what the classics record and civilization reaches, territories the Three Dynasties could not reach—the state has now fully encompassed.
translations.idiomatic: Every land recorded in the classics and touched by civilization, yet beyond the reach of the Three Dynasties, our dynasty now holds in full.

sentences.zh: 此則今日之四境，已逾於夏、殷者也。

translations.literal: Thus today's four borders already exceed those of Xia and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Today's frontiers already surpass those of Xia and Yin.

sentences.zh: 詩人矜薄伐於太原，美化行於江、漢，則是前代之遠裔，而國家之域中。

translations.literal: When the poets boasted of the punitive expedition against Taiyuan, and civilization flourished along the Yangtze and Han—these were distant peripheries of former ages, yet domains within the state's heartland.
translations.idiomatic: When poets praised the punitive campaign against Taiyuan and civilization spread along the Yangtze and Han, those were distant marches of earlier ages—yet heartland domains of our state.

sentences.zh: 至前漢時，匈奴無歳不陷邊，殺掠吏人。

translations.literal: By the Former Han, the Xiongnu raided the borders every year without fail, killing and plundering officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Former Han the Xiongnu breached the frontier every single year, killing and plundering officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 後漢則西羌侵軼漢中，東寇三輔，入河東上黨，幾至洛陽。

translations.literal: In Later Han the Western Qiang raided Hanzhong in the west, struck the Three Adjuncts in the east, entered Hedong and Shangdang, and nearly reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Han the Western Qiang overran Hanzhong, struck the capital region from the east, pushed into Hedong and Shangdang, and nearly reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，則陛下今日之士宇，過於漢朝遠矣。

translations.literal: From this it follows that Your Majesty's territory today far surpasses the Han dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that Your Majesty's realm today far exceeds that of the Han.

sentences.zh: 若其用武荒外，邀功絶域，竭府庫之實，以爭磽確不毛之地，得其人不足以增賦，獲其土不可以耕織。

translations.literal: If one applies military force in the wild borderlands, seeks merit in remote regions, exhausts the treasury's substance to contend for barren, sterile ground—the people gained would not suffice to increase taxes, the land taken could not be tilled or woven upon.
translations.idiomatic: If we wage war in the outer wastes, chase glory in distant lands, and drain the treasury to seize barren ground, the people won would not pay enough tax to matter and the soil could neither be farmed nor woven from.

sentences.zh: 苟求冠帶遠夷之稱，不務固本安人之術，此秦皇、漢武之所行，非五帝、三皇之事業也。

translations.literal: If one merely seeks the fame of bringing distant barbarians into the fold of cap and sash, and does not devote oneself to the art of strengthening the root and settling the people—this is what Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi did, not the enterprise of the Five Emperors and Three Sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: If we chase the empty honor of civilizing distant tribes while neglecting the work of strengthening the root and settling the people, we follow Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi—not the way of the sage emperors.

sentences.zh: 若使越荒外以爲限，竭資財以騁欲，非但不愛人力，亦所以失天心也。

translations.literal: If one crosses beyond the wastelands to set limits, exhausts resources to indulge desire—not only does one fail to cherish human labor, one also loses Heaven's favor thereby.
translations.idiomatic: To push beyond the wastes and spend the treasury to satisfy ambition is not only to waste human labor—it is to lose Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 昔始皇窮兵極武，以求廣地，男子不得耕於野，女子不得蠶於室，長城之下，死者如亂麻，於是天下潰叛。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin Shihuang exhausted troops and pushed warfare to the utmost to broaden territory; men could not plow in the fields, women could not raise silkworms at home; beneath the Great Wall the dead lay like tangled hemp—and then the realm collapsed in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang drove armies to exhaustion to expand his domain; men could not farm, women could not raise silkworms; beneath the Great Wall the dead piled like tangled hemp—and the realm rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 漢武追高、文之宿憤，藉四帝之儲實，於是定朝鮮，討西域，平南越，擊匈奴，府庫空虛，盜賊蜂起，百姓嫁妻賣子，流離於道路者萬計。

translations.literal: Han Wudi pursued the longstanding grievances of Emperor Gao and Emperor Wen, drawing on the stored wealth of four reigns; then he settled Korea, campaigned in the Western Regions, pacified Southern Yue, struck the Xiongnu; the treasuries ran empty, bandits rose like bees, and common people sold wives and children—those wandering destitute on the roads numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi vented the old grievances of Emperors Gao and Wen and spent the hoarded wealth of four reigns conquering Korea, campaigning in the Western Regions, pacifying Southern Yue, and striking the Xiongnu; the treasuries emptied, bandits swarmed, and tens of thousands of people sold wives and children and wandered destitute on the roads.

sentences.zh: 末年覺悟，息兵罷役，封丞相爲富民侯，故能爲天所祐也。

translations.literal: In his late years he awakened, halted troops and ended corvée, enfeoffed his chancellor as Marquis Who Enriches the People—and thus could receive Heaven's protection.
translations.idiomatic: Only in his last years did he see his error, halt the armies, end corvée, and enfeoff his chancellor as Marquis Who Enriches the People—thereby winning Heaven's protection.

sentences.zh: 昔人有言：「與覆車同軌者未嘗安。」

translations.literal: Someone once said: "Those who follow the track of an overturned cart have never been secure.
translations.idiomatic: As someone once said: "Those who follow the ruts of an overturned cart never ride safely."

sentences.zh: 此言雖小，可以喻大。

translations.literal: This saying is small, but can illustrate great matters.
translations.idiomatic: The saying is small, but it speaks to great matters.

sentences.zh: 近者國家頻歳出師，所費滋廣，西戍四鎮，東戍安東，調發日加，百姓虛弊。

translations.literal: Recently the state has sent troops out year after year; expense grows ever greater; garrisoning the Four Garrisons in the west and Andong in the east; levies increase daily; the people are drained and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the state has sent armies out year after year at ever greater cost, garrisoning the Four Garrisons in the west and Andong in the east; levies mount daily and the people are hollowed out.

sentences.zh: 開守西域，事等石田，費用不支，有損無益，轉輸靡絶，杼軸殆空。

translations.literal: Opening and holding the Western Regions is like farming stone fields—costs cannot be sustained, harm without benefit; transport supplies never cease; the looms are nearly empty.
translations.idiomatic: Opening and holding the Western Regions is like tilling rock—costs cannot be borne, losses outweigh gains, transport never stops, and the looms stand nearly idle.

sentences.zh: 越磧逾海，分兵防守，行役既久，怨曠亦多。

translations.literal: Crossing deserts and seas, dividing troops for defense—service has been long, and resentment and separation are many.
translations.idiomatic: Troops cross deserts and seas on divided garrison duty; service drags on, and resentment and long separation multiply.

sentences.zh: 昔詩人云：「王事靡盬，不能藝稷黍。」

translations.literal: The poets of old said: "King's service never rests; we cannot plant millet and grain."
translations.idiomatic: The poets of old sang: "The king's service never ends; we cannot plant millet and grain."

sentences.zh: 「 豈不懷歸，畏此罪罟。

translations.literal: Would we not yearn to return? We fear this net of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: "Would we not long to go home? We fear the snare of punishment.

sentences.zh: 念彼蒸人，涕零如雨。」

translations.literal: Thinking of those common folk, tears fall like rain."
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of those common people, tears fall like rain."

sentences.zh: 此則前代怨思之辭也。

translations.literal: This is the language of resentment and longing from former ages.
translations.idiomatic: These are the words of resentment and longing from ages past.

sentences.zh: 上不是恤，則政不行而邪氣作；

translations.literal: If the ruler above does not remedy and care for this, then government fails and malign influences arise;
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler above does not set things right, government fails and malign forces arise;

sentences.zh: 邪氣作，則蟲螟生而水旱起。

translations.literal: when malign influences arise, locusts and borers appear and flood and drought begin.
translations.idiomatic: when malign forces arise, locusts and borers appear and flood and drought follow.

sentences.zh: 若此，雖禱祀百神，不能調陰陽矣。

translations.literal: If matters are thus, though one pray to the hundred spirits, one cannot harmonize yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: When things reach this point, prayer to the hundred spirits cannot restore the balance of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 方今關東饑饉，蜀、漢逃亡，江、淮以南，徵求不息。

translations.literal: At present there is famine east of the Pass; in Shu and Han people flee; south of the Yangtze and Huai, exactions never cease.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Pass there is famine; in Shu and Han people flee; south of the Yangtze and Huai exactions never stop.

sentences.zh: 人不復業，則相率爲盜，本根一搖，憂患不淺。

translations.literal: If people cannot return to their livelihoods, they will band together as bandits; once the root is shaken, the woes will not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: If people cannot return to their trades they will turn to banditry in groups; once the root is shaken, the troubles will be grave.

sentences.zh: 其所以然者，皆爲遠戍方外，以竭中國，爭蠻貊不毛之地，乖子養蒼生之道也。

translations.literal: The reason for all this is that garrisoning distant outer regions exhausts China, contending for the barren lands of the Man and Mo—it violates the way of nourishing the common people as one's children.
translations.idiomatic: The cause of all this is distant garrisoning beyond the borders, draining the heartland to fight over barren tribal lands—a betrayal of the ruler's duty to nurture the people as his children.

sentences.zh: 昔漢元納賈捐之之謀而罷珠崖郡，宣帝用魏相之策而棄車師之田，豈不欲慕尚虛名，蓋憚勞人力也。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Yuandi accepted Jia Juanzhi's plan and abolished Zhuya commandery; Xuandi employed Wei Xiang's strategy and abandoned the fields of Jushi—they did not wish to pursue empty fame; they feared exhausting human labor.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Yuan of Han took Jia Juanzhi's advice and abolished Zhuya commandery, and Emperor Xuan followed Wei Xiang's counsel and gave up the fields of Jushi—not because they scorned glory, but because they feared wasting human labor.

sentences.zh: 近貞觀年中，克平九姓，冊李思摩爲可汗，使統諸部者，蓋以夷狄叛則伐之，降則撫之，得推亡固存之義，無遠戍勞人之役。

translations.literal: Recently in the Zhenguan era, after subduing the Nine Surnames, Li Simo was enthroned as qaghan to command the various tribes—this was because when the Yi and Di rebel, strike them; when they submit, soothe them—realizing the principle of supporting what is dying and preserving what remains, without the corvée of distant garrisoning that burdens the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent Zhenguan era, after defeating the Nine Surnames, Li Simo was enthroned as qaghan to rule the tribes—rebel and you strike them, submit and you soothe them—honoring the principle of preserving what survives without the corvée of distant garrisons.

sentences.zh: 此則近日之令典，經邊之故事。

translations.literal: This is the recent exemplary standard, the established precedent of border governance.
translations.idiomatic: This is the recent model and the established precedent of frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 竊見阿史那斛瑟羅，陰山貴種，代雄沙漠，若委之四鎮，使統諸蕃，封爲可汗，遣禦寇患，則國家有繼絶之美，荒外無轉輸之役。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that Ashina Queshelo, noble stock of the Yin Mountains, generations heroic in the desert—if entrusted with the Four Garrisons to command the various tribes, enfeoffed as qaghan to repel invaders—the state would have the glory of continuing what was cut off, and the outer wastes would have no transport corvée.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Ashina Queshelo, noble stock of the Yin Mountains and a desert chieftain for generations, if entrusted with the Four Garrisons to rule the tribes and enfeoffed as qaghan to repel invaders, would bring the state the honor of restoring a broken line and spare the outer wastes endless transport corvée.

sentences.zh: 如臣所見，請捐四鎮以肥中國，罷安東以實遼西，省軍費於遠方，並甲兵於塞上，則恒、代之鎮重，而邊州之備實矣。

translations.literal: As your subject sees it, please relinquish the Four Garrisons to enrich China, abolish Andong to strengthen Liaoxi, save military costs in distant places, and concentrate armor and troops on the frontier—then the garrisons of Heng and Dai will be weighty, and border prefectures' defenses solid.
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, relinquish the Four Garrisons to enrich the heartland, abolish Andong to strengthen Liaoxi, cut military costs in distant lands, and mass armor and troops on the frontier—then the Heng and Dai garrisons will gain weight and the border prefectures real strength.

sentences.zh: 況綏撫夷狄，蓋防其越逸，無侵侮之患則可矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, in soothing the Yi and Di, one need only guard against their overstepping—if there is no harassment or insult, that is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: In pacifying the barbarians one need only keep them from overstepping; if they do not harass or insult us, that is enough.

sentences.zh: 何必窮其窟穴，與螻蟻計校長短哉！

translations.literal: Why must one exhaust their nests and measure strength against ants!
translations.idiomatic: Why must we hunt them to their lairs and measure strength against ants!

sentences.zh: 且王者外寧必有內憂，蓋爲不勤修政故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when kings find outer peace, inner trouble must arise—because they fail to diligently cultivate government.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler finds peace abroad, trouble at home follows—because he has neglected to govern diligently.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下棄之度外，無以絶域未平爲念。

translations.literal: Humbly, may Your Majesty set distant regions beyond concern and not fix your mind on unrest in remote lands.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask Your Majesty to set distant regions aside and not fix your mind on pacifying the outer wastes.

sentences.zh: 但當敕邊兵謹守備，蓄銳以待敵，待其自至，然後擊之，此李牧所以製匈奴也。

translations.literal: You need only instruct frontier troops to guard defenses carefully, store keen edge to await the enemy, wait until they come of themselves, then strike—this is how Li Mu controlled the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: You need only order frontier troops to hold their defenses, store their strength, wait for the enemy to come to them, and then strike—this is how Li Mu mastered the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 當今所要者，莫若令邊城警守備，遠斥候，聚軍實，蓄威武。

translations.literal: What is needed today is, above all, to have border cities alert their defenses, post distant scouts, gather military stores, and store martial might.
translations.idiomatic: What is needed now, above all, is to alert the border cities, post distant scouts, stock military supplies, and store martial power.

sentences.zh: 以逸待勞，則戰士力倍；

translations.literal: Awaiting the weary with rested men, warriors' strength doubles;
translations.idiomatic: Meet the weary with rested men and warriors fight at double strength;

sentences.zh: 以主禦客，則我得其便；

translations.literal: defending as host against a guest, we gain advantage;
translations.idiomatic: fight as host against guest and we hold the advantage;

sentences.zh: 堅壁清野，則寇無所得。

translations.literal: with strong walls and cleared fields, invaders gain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: hold strong walls and clear the countryside and invaders gain nothing.

sentences.zh: 自然賊深入必有顛躓之慮，淺入必無虜獲之益。

translations.literal: Naturally if bandits penetrate deeply they will have fear of stumbling; if they penetrate shallowly they will surely gain no benefit of capture.
translations.idiomatic: Invaders who push deep will fear disaster; those who raid shallowly will gain no plunder worth the effort.

sentences.zh: 如此數年，可使二虜不擊而服矣。

translations.literal: Thus within several years, the two barbarian foes could be made to submit without a blow.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the two barbarian enemies could be made to submit without a blow being struck.

sentences.zh: 仁傑又請廢安東，復高氏爲君長，停江南之轉輸，慰河北之勞弊，數年之後，可以安人富國。

translations.literal: Renjie also requested abolishing Andong, restoring the Gao clan as tribal chief, halting transport levies from south of the Yangtze, easing the labor and exhaustion of Hebei—within several years, people could be settled and the state enriched.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie also asked to abolish Andong, restore the Gao clan as tribal chiefs, halt transport levies from south of the Yangtze, and ease Hebei's exhaustion—within a few years the people could be settled and the state enriched.

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，識者是之。

translations.literal: Though the proposal was not adopted, those who understood approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not adopted, but those who understood the issue approved it.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校納言，兼右肅政臺御史大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed acting Director of Edicts and concurrently Censor-in-Chief of the Right Suheng Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting director of edicts and concurrently censor-in-chief of the Right Suheng Office.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，突厥侵掠趙、定等州，命仁傑爲河北道元帥，以便宜從事。

translations.literal: At the start of the Shengli era, the Turks raided Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures; Renjie was ordered to be commander of the Hebei circuit, with discretion to act as needed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shengli era the Turks raided Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures; Renjie was appointed commander of the Hebei circuit with full discretion.

sentences.zh: 突厥盡殺所掠男女萬餘人，從五回道而去。

translations.literal: The Turks slaughtered all the more than ten thousand men and women they had seized and departed via the Wuhui route.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks killed every one of the more than ten thousand men and women they had seized and withdrew by the Wuhui route.

sentences.zh: 仁傑總兵十萬追之不及。

translations.literal: Renjie mustered a hundred thousand troops but could not catch them.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie led a hundred thousand men in pursuit but could not overtake them.

sentences.zh: 便製仁傑河北道安撫大使。

translations.literal: An edict immediately made Renjie Pacification Commissioner of the Hebei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict at once appointed him pacification commissioner of the Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 時河朔人庶，多爲突厥逼脅，賊退後懼誅，又多逃匿。

translations.literal: At the time the people of north Hebei had largely been coerced by the Turks; after the bandits withdrew they feared execution and many went into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Many people north of the Yellow River had been forced to serve the Turks; after the raiders withdrew they feared punishment and went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 仁傑上疏曰：臣聞朝廷議者，以爲契丹作梗，始明人之逆順，或因迫脅，或有願從，或受偽官，或爲招慰，或兼外賊，或是土人，跡雖不同，心則無別。誠以山東雄猛，由來重氣，一顧之勢，至死不回。近緣軍機，調發傷重，家道悉破，或至逃亡，剔屋賣田，人不爲售，內顧生計，四壁皆空。重以官典侵漁，因事而起，取其髓腦，曾無心愧。修築池城，繕造兵甲，州縣役使，十倍軍機。官司不矜，期之必取，枷杖之下，痛切肌膚。事迫情危，不循禮義，愁苦之地，不樂其生。有利則歸，且圖賒死，此乃君子之愧辱，小人之常行。人猶水也，壅之則爲泉，疏之則爲川，通塞隨流，豈有常性。昔董卓之亂，神器播遷，及卓被誅，部曲無赦，事窮變起，毒害生人，京室丘墟，化爲禾黍。此由恩不普洽，失在機先。臣一讀此書，未嘗不廢卷歎息。今以負罪之伍，必不在家，露宿草行，潛竄山澤。赦之則出，不赦則狂，山東群盜，緣茲聚結。臣以邊塵暫起，不足爲憂，中土不安，以此爲事。臣聞持大國者不可以小道，理事廣者不可以細分。人主恢弘，不拘常法，罪之則眾情恐懼，恕之則反側自安。伏願曲赦河北諸州，一無所問。自然人神道暢，率土歡心，諸軍凱旋，得無侵擾。

translations.literal: Renjie submitted a memorial, saying: I have heard that those who deliberate at court think that when the Khitan made trouble, people's loyalty or rebellion was thereby made clear: some were coerced, some willingly followed, some accepted false offices, some served in recruitment and pacification, some joined with the foreign enemy, and some were local people. Though the traces differed, their hearts were no different. Truly, the men of Shandong are fierce and bold and have always valued spirit; once committed, they do not turn back even unto death. Recently, because of military needs, requisitions and mobilizations have been grievously heavy, household resources have been entirely ruined, and some have even fled. They stripped houses and sold fields, but no one would buy; looking within at their livelihood, the four walls were empty. Added to this, officials and clerks encroached and plundered, taking advantage of events as they arose, extracting their marrow and brains without the slightest shame. Repairing moats and walls, making armor and weapons, and service imposed by prefectures and counties were ten times worse than the military needs themselves. The offices showed no pity and demanded payment by deadline; under cangues and cudgels the pain cut flesh and skin. With affairs urgent and feelings endangered, they did not follow ritual and righteousness; in a place of grief and hardship, they found no joy in living. If there was advantage, they submitted, merely planning to postpone death. This is shameful to gentlemen, but the common conduct of petty men. People are like water: block it and it becomes a spring; dredge it and it becomes a river. Its flow follows opening or blockage; how could it have a constant nature? Formerly, in Dong Zhuo's disorder, the imperial regalia was moved away, and when Zhuo was executed, his troops received no amnesty. With matters exhausted, change arose; they poisoned and harmed the living people, and the capital became mounds and ruins, transformed into grain fields. This came from grace not being broadly extended and the failure lying before the moment of crisis. Whenever your subject reads this account, I never fail to put down the scroll and sigh. Now those bearing guilt certainly do not remain at home; they sleep in the open, move through the grass, and hide in mountains and marshes. If they are pardoned, they will come out; if they are not pardoned, they will go mad, and the bandits of Shandong will gather because of this. Your subject considers a temporary rising of border dust not worth worrying over; the central lands being unsettled is what must be treated as the matter. I have heard that one who holds a great state cannot use petty methods, and one who orders broad affairs cannot divide them finely. A ruler of men is broad and expansive and is not bound by ordinary laws. Punish them, and the feelings of the masses will be fearful; forgive them, and the unsettled will become secure of themselves. I humbly ask that a special pardon be given to the prefectures of Hebei, with nothing at all inquired into. Naturally the way of men and spirits will flow freely, all within the lands will rejoice, the armies will return in triumph, and there will be no infringement or disturbance.

sentences.zh: 製從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress approved it.

sentences.zh: 軍還，授內史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was appointed director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 聖曆三年，則天幸三陽宮，王公百僚鹹經侍從，唯仁傑特賜宅一區，當時恩寵無比。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengli, Wu Zetian visited the Sanyang Palace; nobles and the hundred officials all attended in retinue, but Renjie alone was specially granted one residence—favor unmatched at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shengli Wu Zetian visited the Sanyang Palace; nobles and officials all attended, but Renjie alone received a special grant of a residence—favor without equal at the time.

sentences.zh: 是歳六月，左玉鈐衞大將軍李楷固、右武威衞將軍駱務整討契丹餘眾，擒之，獻俘於含樞殿。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month, Left Grand General of the Jade Bridle Guard Regiment Li Kaigu and Right General of the Martial Might Guard Regiment Luo Wuzheng attacked remaining Khitan forces, captured them, and presented captives at the Hall of the Pivot of Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month Left Grand General Li Kaigu of the Jade Bridle Guard and Right General Luo Wuzheng of the Martial Might Guard attacked the remaining Khitan forces, captured them, and presented prisoners at the Hall of the Pivot of Harmony.

sentences.zh: 則天大悅，特賜楷固姓武氏。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian was greatly pleased and specially granted Kaigu the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian was greatly pleased and specially granted Kaigu the surname Wu.

sentences.zh: 楷固、務整，並契丹李盡忠之別帥也。

translations.literal: Kaigu and Wuzheng were both subordinate commanders of the Khitan Li Jinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Kaigu and Wuzheng had both been subordinate commanders under the Khitan leader Li Jinzhong.

sentences.zh: 初，盡忠之作亂，楷固等屢率兵以陷官軍，後兵敗來降，有司斷以極法。

translations.literal: Initially when Jinzhong rebelled, Kaigu and others repeatedly led troops to defeat government forces; later, defeated, they came to surrender; the office ruled capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinzhong first rebelled, Kaigu and the others had repeatedly led troops against the imperial armies; after defeat they surrendered, and the authorities ruled death.

sentences.zh: 仁傑議以爲楷固等並有驍將之才，若恕其死，必能感恩效節。

translations.literal: Renjie argued that Kaigu and the others all possessed talent as fierce generals—if their deaths were forgiven, they would surely repay with gratitude and loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie argued that Kaigu and the others were fierce generals of real talent; if spared, they would repay the grace with loyal service.

sentences.zh: 又奏請授其官爵，委以專征。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting grants of office and rank, entrusting them with independent command.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized asking that they be given office and rank and entrusted with independent command.

sentences.zh: 製並從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 及楷固等凱旋，則天召仁傑預宴，因舉觴親勸，歸賞於仁傑。

translations.literal: When Kaigu and the others returned in triumph, Wu Zetian summoned Renjie to the feast, raised a cup and personally urged him to drink, attributing the reward to Renjie.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaigu and the others returned in triumph, Wu Zetian summoned Renjie to the feast, raised her cup and urged him to drink, and credited the victory to him.

sentences.zh: 授楷固左玉鈐衞大將軍，賜爵燕國公。

translations.literal: Kaigu was appointed Left Grand General of the Jade Bridle Guard Regiment and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Kaigu was made left grand general of the Jade Bridle Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 則天又將造大像，用功數百萬，令天下僧尼每日人出一錢，以助成之。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian was also about to build a great Buddha image, requiring millions of work-days; she ordered monks and nuns throughout the realm to contribute one coin per person daily to help complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian was also planning a great Buddha image that would require millions of work-days; she ordered every monk and nun in the realm to contribute one coin per day toward its completion.

sentences.zh: 仁傑上疏諫曰：臣聞爲政之本，必先人事。陛下矜群生迷謬，溺喪無歸，欲令像教兼行，睹相生善。非爲塔廟必欲崇奢，豈令僧尼皆須檀施？得栰尚舍，而況其餘。今之伽藍，製過宮闕，窮奢極壯，畫繢盡工，寶珠殫於綴飾，環材竭於輪奐。工不使鬼，止在役人，物不天來，終須地出，不損百姓，將何以求？生之有時，用之無度，編戸所奉，常若不充，痛切肌膚，不辭箠楚。遊僧一説，矯陳禍福，翦發解衣，仍慚其少。亦有離間骨肉，事均路人，身自納妻，謂無彼我。皆托佛法，詿誤生人。裏陌動有經坊，闤闠亦立精舍。化誘倍急，切於官征；法事所須，嚴於製敕。膏腴美業，倍取其多；水碾莊園，數亦非少。逃丁避罪，並集法門，無名之僧，凡有幾萬，都下檢括，已得數千。且一夫不耕，猶受其弊，浮食者眾，又劫人財。臣每思惟，實所悲痛。往在江表，像法盛興，梁武、簡文，舍施無限。及其三淮沸浪，五嶺騰煙。列刹盈衢，無救危亡之禍；緇衣蔽路，豈有勤王之師！比年已來，風塵屢擾，水旱不節，征役稍繁。家業先空，瘡痍未復，此時興役，力所未堪，伏惟聖朝，功德無量，何必要營大像，而以勞費爲名。雖斂僧錢，百未支一。尊容既廣，不可露居，覆以百層，尚憂未遍，自餘廓廡，不得全無。又雲不損國財，不傷百姓，以此事主，可謂盡忠？臣今思惟，兼采眾議，鹹以爲如來設教，以慈悲爲主，下濟群品，應是本心，豈欲勞人，以存虛飾？當今有事，邊境未寧，宜寬征鎮之徭，省不急之費。設令雇作，皆以利趨，既失田時，自然棄本。今不樹稼，來歳必饑，役在其中，難以取給。況無官助，義無得成，若費官財，又盡人力，一隅有難，將何救之！

translations.literal: Renjie submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: I have heard that the root of governance must first be human affairs. Your Majesty pities the delusion and error of the living masses, drowning and lost with nowhere to return, and wishes to have the teaching of images practiced alongside other teachings, so that people may see images and produce goodness. But it is not that stupas and temples must be exalted in extravagance, nor that monks and nuns all must receive alms. If even the raft is to be abandoned once gained, how much more the rest? The monasteries of today exceed palaces in their regulations, exhaust extravagance and reach utmost magnificence, have paintings and decorations worked to the limit of craft, deplete precious pearls for ornamentation, and exhaust fine timber for splendor. Work is not done by spirits; it only lies in employing people. Materials do not come from Heaven; in the end they must come from the earth. If the common people are not diminished, how will these things be obtained? Living things have their proper seasons, but expenditures have no measure. What registered households provide always seems insufficient; though pain cuts flesh and skin, they do not refuse whips and beatings. A wandering monk gives one explanation, falsely setting out fortune and misfortune; people cut their hair and remove their clothes and still feel ashamed that it is too little. There are also those who estrange bone and flesh until affairs are equal to those of strangers, who personally take wives and say there is no distinction between self and other. All rely on the Buddhist law and mislead living people. In lanes and wards there are scriptures halls everywhere, and in the markets monasteries too are established. Their transforming enticements are twice as urgent, more pressing than official levies; what ritual services require is stricter than imperial commands. Fertile and beautiful properties are taken in multiplied amounts; water mills, estates, and gardens are also not few. Fugitives from labor service and those avoiding guilt all gather at the gate of the law; nameless monks number many tens of thousands, and in checks under the capital several thousand have already been found. Moreover, if one man does not plow, others still suffer the harm; when many eat without producing, they also rob others of wealth. Whenever your subject thinks on this, it is truly what pains and grieves me. Formerly south of the Yangtze, the image teaching flourished greatly; Emperor Wu and Emperor Jianwen of Liang gave alms without limit. When the three Huai boiled with waves and the Five Ranges rose in smoke, rows of temples filled the avenues but did not save them from the disaster of danger and ruin; black-robed monks covered the roads, but where were the armies diligent for the king? In recent years, war dust has repeatedly disturbed us, floods and droughts have been irregular, and campaigns and labor services have gradually grown burdensome. Household livelihoods were already empty, wounds have not yet healed, and to raise labor service at this time is more than strength can bear. I humbly think that the merit and virtue of the sacred court are immeasurable, so why must it build a great image and take toil and expense as its name? Even if monks' money is collected, it will not cover one part in a hundred. Since the honored image is broad, it cannot dwell exposed; even if covered with a hundred stories, one would still fear it was not complete, and the remaining corridors and side buildings could not be entirely absent. It is also said that this will not diminish state wealth or harm the common people. To serve one's ruler by this affair, can it be called utmost loyalty? Your subject has now thought this over and also gathered the opinions of many, and all consider that when the Thus Come One established his teaching, he took compassion and mercy as its root and rescuing all beings below as his original heart. How could he have wished to weary people in order to preserve empty ornament? At present there are affairs, and the borders are not yet pacified. It is fitting to ease the labor services of campaigns and garrisons and reduce expenses that are not urgent. Even if workers are hired, all pursue profit; once they miss the farming season, they naturally abandon the root. If crops are not planted now, next year there will surely be hunger. With labor service lying in the midst of this, it will be difficult to obtain supplies. Moreover, without official assistance, by principle it cannot be completed; if official wealth is spent and the people's strength is also exhausted, when one corner has trouble, how will it be rescued?

sentences.zh: 則天乃罷其役。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian then halted the project.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian then halted the project.

sentences.zh: 是歳九月，病卒，則天爲之舉哀，廢朝三日，贈文昌右相，諡曰文惠。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month he died of illness; Wu Zetian mourned for him, suspended court for three days, posthumously appointed him Vice Director of Right of the Palace of Literary Brilliance, posthumous name Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month he died of illness; Wu Zetian mourned him, suspended court for three days, posthumously made him vice director of right of the Palace of Literary Brilliance, and gave him the posthumous name Wenhui, Cultured and Beneficent.

sentences.zh: 仁傑常以舉賢爲意，其所引拔桓彥範、敬暉、竇懷貞、姚崇等，至公卿者數十人。

translations.literal: Renjie constantly made recommending the worthy his purpose; those he advanced—Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Dou Huaizhen, Yao Chong, and others—who reached ministerial rank numbered in the dozens.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie always made recommending talent his aim; among those he advanced to ministerial rank—Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Dou Huaizhen, Yao Chong, and others—were dozens of men.

sentences.zh: 初，則天嘗問仁傑曰：「朕要一好漢任使，有乎？」

translations.literal: Initially Wu Zetian once asked Renjie: "I need a capable man to employ—is there one?
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu Zetian asked Renjie: "I need a capable man to employ—is there one?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「陛下作何任使？」

translations.literal: Renjie said: "For what purpose does Your Majesty wish to employ him?"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said: "For what post does Your Majesty wish to use him?"

sentences.zh: 則天曰：「朕欲待以將相。」

translations.literal: Wu Zetian said: "I wish to treat him as a general or minister."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian said: "I mean to use him as a general or minister."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣料陛下若求文章資歴，則今之宰臣李嶠、蘇味道亦足爲文吏矣。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject surmises that if Your Majesty seeks literary credentials and résumé, then the present chancellors Li Jiao and Su Weidao would suffice as literary officials.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "If Your Majesty wants literary credentials and résumé, the present chancellors Li Jiao and Su Weidao would suffice as literary officials.

sentences.zh: 豈非文士齷齪，思得奇才用之，以成天下之務者乎？」

translations.literal: Is it not that literary men seem petty, and you wish to obtain an exceptional talent to use in completing the affairs of the realm?"」
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that literary men seem too narrow, and you wish to find an exceptional talent to carry out the affairs of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 則天悅曰：「此朕心也。」

translations.literal: Empress Zetian, pleased, said: 「This is my own mind as well.」
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was delighted and said, "That is exactly what I have in mind."

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「荊州長史張柬之，其人雖老，真宰相才也。

translations.literal: Ren Jie said: 「Zhang Jianzhi, the prefectural secretary of Jingzhou—though the man is old, he is truly talent for chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie replied, "Zhang Jianzhi, the prefectural secretary of Jingzhou, is advanced in years, but he is genuine chancellor material.

sentences.zh: 且久不遇，若用之，必盡節於國家矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, he has long gone without opportunity; if employed, he will surely exhaust his loyalty to the state.」
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he has long gone unrecognized; if you appoint him, he will surely devote himself utterly to the realm."

sentences.zh: 則天乃召拜洛州司馬。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian then summoned and appointed him Vice Marshal of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The empress thereupon summoned Zhang Jianzhi and appointed him Vice Marshal of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 他日，又求賢。

translations.literal: On another day, she again sought worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion she again asked for recommendations of able men.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「臣前言張柬之，猶未用也。」

translations.literal: Renjie said: "Your subject previously spoke of Zhang Jianzhi, yet he has still not been employed.」
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "Your subject spoke earlier of Zhang Jianzhi, yet he still has not been properly used."

sentences.zh: 則天曰：「已遷之矣。」

translations.literal: Empress Zetian said: 「I have already transferred him.」
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said, "I have already moved him to another post."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣薦之爲相，今爲洛州司馬，非用之也。」

translations.literal: He replied: 「Your subject recommended him to be chancellor; now he is Vice Marshal of Luozhou—this is not employing him.」
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your subject recommended him as chancellor, yet he is now Vice Marshal of Luozhou—that is not putting him to use."

sentences.zh: 又遷爲秋官侍郎，後竟召爲相。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice, and in the end was summoned to be chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was then transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, and was eventually summoned to serve as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 柬之果能興復中宗，蓋仁傑之推薦也。

translations.literal: Jianzhi indeed was able to restore Zhongzong—this was due to Ren Jie's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: That Jianzhi was able to restore Emperor Zhongzong was owed, in the end, to Renjie's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 仁傑嘗爲魏州刺史，人吏爲立生祠。

translations.literal: Ren Jie once served as prefect of Weizhou, and officials and commoners built a living shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Renjie had served as prefect of Weizhou, the people and officials erected a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 及去職，其子景暉爲魏州司功參軍，頗貪暴，爲人所惡，乃毀仁傑之祠。

translations.literal: When he left office, his son Jinghui was Revenue Assistant of Weizhou, quite greedy and violent, hated by people, and so destroyed Ren Jie's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: After Renjie left office, his son Jinghui served as Revenue Assistant in Weizhou. Jinghui was greedy and brutal and widely despised, and the people tore down Renjie's shrine.

sentences.zh: 長子光嗣，聖曆初爲司府丞，則天令宰相各舉尚書郎一人，仁傑乃薦光嗣。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guangsi, at the beginning of the Shengli era, was Commissioner of the Palace Revenues Office. Empress Zetian ordered each chancellor to recommend one Bureau Director, and Ren Jie then recommended Guangsi.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie's eldest son Guangsi, at the start of the Shengli reign, held the post of Commissioner of the Palace Revenues Office. When Empress Wu ordered each chancellor to nominate one Bureau Director, Renjie recommended Guangsi.

sentences.zh: 拜地官員外郎，蒞事稱職，則天喜而言曰：「祁奚內舉，果得其人。」

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Director in the Ministry of Population Affairs, handled affairs ably, and Empress Zetian, pleased, said: 「Qi Xi recommended from within his family and indeed obtained the right man.」
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi was appointed Assistant Director in the Ministry of Population Affairs and proved competent in office. Empress Wu was pleased and said, "Like Qi Xi recommending a kinsman, you have indeed found the right man."

sentences.zh: 開元七年，自汴州刺史轉揚州大都督府長史，坐贓貶歙州別駕卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, he transferred from prefect of Bianzhou to Chief Secretary of the Yangzhou Grand Protectorate, was convicted of embezzlement, demoted to Vice Prefect of Shezhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan he was transferred from Prefect of Bianzhou to Chief Secretary of the Yangzhou Grand Protectorate; later he was convicted of corruption, demoted to Vice Prefect of Shezhou, and died there.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗在房陵，而吉頊、李昭德皆有匡復讜言，則天無復辟意。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhongzong was at Fangling, Ji Xu and Li Zhaode both had counsel on restoration, yet Empress Zetian had no intent to restore him.
translations.idiomatic: At first, while Emperor Zhongzong was confined at Fangling, both Ji Xu and Li Zhaode offered counsel on restoring him, but Empress Wu showed no inclination to bring him back.

sentences.zh: 唯仁傑每從容奏對，無不以子母恩情爲言，則天亦漸省悟，竟召還中宗，復爲儲貳。

translations.literal: Only Ren Jie, in each unhurried memorial and response, spoke without fail of the affection between mother and son; Empress Zetian also gradually came to understand, and in the end recalled Zhongzong and restored him as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie alone, in every calm memorial and reply, spoke always of the bond between mother and son. Empress Wu gradually came round, and at last recalled Zhongzong and restored him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗自房陵還宮，則天匿之帳中，召仁傑以廬陵爲言。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhongzong returned from Fangling to the palace, Empress Zetian hid him within the canopy tent and summoned Ren Jie, speaking of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong first returned from Fangling to the palace, Empress Wu concealed him behind a screen and summoned Renjie, speaking as though the heir were still Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 仁傑慷慨敷奏，言發涕流，遽出中宗謂仁傑曰：「還卿儲君。」

translations.literal: Ren Jie passionately laid out his memorial, words issuing with flowing tears; she suddenly brought out Zhongzong and said to Ren Jie: 「I return your crown prince to you.」
translations.idiomatic: Renjie spoke with passionate urgency, tears streaming as he pleaded; the empress suddenly produced Zhongzong and said to Renjie, "I give you back your crown prince."

sentences.zh: 仁傑降階泣賀，既已，奏曰：「太子還宮，人無知者，物議安審是非？」
