translations.literal: Ren Jie descended the steps weeping in congratulation; when that was done, he memorialized: 「The crown prince has returned to the palace, yet no one knows of it—how can public opinion judge what is right and wrong?」
translations.idiomatic: Renjie stepped down weeping with joy; when he had composed himself, he memorialized, "The crown prince has returned to the palace, yet no one knows of it—how can public opinion weigh the rights and wrongs of the matter?"

sentences.zh: 則天以爲然，乃復置中宗於龍門，具禮迎歸，人情感悅。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian thought this correct, and so again placed Zhongzong at Longmen, fully prepared the rites to welcome him back, and the people's feelings rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu agreed, and had Zhongzong received again at Longmen with full ceremony. The people were deeply moved and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 仁傑前後匡復奏對，凡數萬言，開元中，北海太守李邕撰爲《梁公別傳》，備載其辭。

translations.literal: Ren Jie's restoration memorials and responses before and after totaled tens of thousands of words; in the Kaiyuan era, Li Yong, prefect of Beihai, compiled them as the Separate Biography of the Duke of Liang, fully recording his words.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie's memorials and replies on the restoration altogether ran to tens of thousands of words. In the Kaiyuan era Li Yong, Prefect of Beihai, compiled them into a Separate Biography of the Duke of Liang, preserving his words in full.

sentences.zh: 中宗返正，追贈司空；

translations.literal: When Zhongzong returned to orthodox rule, Ren Jie was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongzong was restored, Renjie was posthumously honored as Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 睿宗追封梁國公。

translations.literal: Ruizong posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong later posthumously ennobled him as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 仁傑族曾孫兼謨。

translations.literal: Ren Jie's collateral great-great-grandson was Jian Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie's collateral great-great-grandson was Di Jianmo.

sentences.zh: 仁傑族曾孫 兼謨兼謨，登進士第。

translations.literal: Ren Jie's collateral great-great-grandson Jian Mo—Jian Mo passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Di Jianmo, Renjie's collateral great-great-grandson, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 祖郊、父邁，仕官皆微。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jiao and his father Mai both held minor official posts.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiao and his father Mai had both held only minor offices.

sentences.zh: 兼謨元和末解褐襄陽推官，試校書郎，言行剛正，使府知名。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era Jian Mo began his career as investigating officer of Xiangyang and provisional collator; his conduct and words were upright, and he became known in the military governor's office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe reign Jianmo entered service as investigating officer in Xiangyang and as provisional collator. Upright in word and deed, he won a name for himself in the governor's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 憲宗召爲左拾遺，累上書言事，歴尚書郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong summoned him as Left Reminder; he repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of state and served as Bureau Director.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong summoned him to serve as Left Reminder. He memorialized repeatedly on affairs of state and rose through posts as Bureau Director.

sentences.zh: 長慶、太和中，歴鄭州刺史，以治行稱，入爲給事中。

translations.literal: In the Changqing and Taihe eras he served as prefect of Zhengzhou, was famed for his governance, and entered court as Attendant Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing and Taihe reigns he served as Prefect of Zhengzhou, where his administration won praise, and was then recalled to court as Attendant Expositor.

sentences.zh: 開成初，度支左藏庫妄破漬汙縑帛等贓罪，文宗以事在赦前不理。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng, the Left Treasury of the Revenue Ministry wantonly destroyed stained and spoiled silk goods and the like in an embezzlement case; Emperor Wenzong, because the matter predated an amnesty, did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng reign officials in the Left Treasury of the Revenue Ministry wantonly destroyed stained and spoiled silk in connection with an embezzlement case. Emperor Wenzong declined to prosecute because the offense predated a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 兼謨封還敕書，文宗召而諭之曰：「嘉卿舉職，然朕已赦其長官，典吏亦宜在宥。

translations.literal: Jian Mo sealed and returned the edict. Emperor Wenzong summoned and instructed him: 「I commend you for performing your duty, yet I have already pardoned the chief official, and the clerks too should be within forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo sealed the edict and returned it unread. Emperor Wenzong summoned him and said, "I commend you for doing your duty, but I have already pardoned the chief official, and the clerks should be forgiven as well.

sentences.zh: 然事或不可，卿勿以封敕爲艱。」

translations.literal: Yet if the matter cannot be so, do not regard sealing and returning an edict as difficult.」
translations.idiomatic: If the matter truly cannot stand, however, you must not shrink from returning an edict unexecuted."

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 謝日，文宗顧謂之曰：「御史臺朝廷綱紀，臺綱正則朝廷理，朝廷正則天下理。

translations.literal: On the day he thanked the throne, Emperor Wenzong turned to him and said: 「The Censorate is the disciplinary cord of the court; if the censorate's cord is straight, the court is governed; if the court is straight, the realm is governed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he thanked the throne, Emperor Wenzong turned to him and said, "The Censorate is the disciplinary backbone of the court. When its standards are upright, the court is well ordered; when the court is well ordered, the realm is well ordered.

sentences.zh: 凡執法者，大抵以畏忌顧望爲心，職業由茲不舉。

translations.literal: All who enforce the law, for the most part, take fear and hesitation as their guiding motive, and their duties thereby go unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Those charged with enforcing the law are, for the most part, ruled by fear and hesitation, and so fail in their duties.

sentences.zh: 卿梁公之後，自有家法，豈復爲常常之心哉！」

translations.literal: You are a descendant of the Duke of Liang and have your own family standards—how could you again harbor an ordinary mind!」
translations.idiomatic: You are a descendant of the Duke of Liang and carry your family's standards in your blood. Surely you will not settle for the timid habits of ordinary men!"

sentences.zh: 兼謨謝曰：「朝法或未得中，臣固悉心彈奏。」

translations.literal: Jian Mo thanked him and said: 「If court law has not yet hit the mark, your subject will wholeheartedly impeach.」
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo thanked him and replied, "If the court's handling of the law falls short, your subject will impeach without reserve."

sentences.zh: 會江西觀察使吳士矩違額加給軍士，破官錢數十萬計。

translations.literal: It happened that Wu Shiju, observation commissioner of Jiangxi, exceeded the allotted amount in supplementary payments to soldiers and spent several hundred thousand in government funds.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward Wu Shiju, Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi, paid soldiers above the authorized quota and squandered several hundred thousand strings of government money.

sentences.zh: 兼謨奏曰：「觀察使守陛下土地，宣陛下詔條，臨戎賞軍，州有定數。

translations.literal: Jian Mo memorialized: 「An observation commissioner guards Your Majesty's lands and proclaims Your Majesty's regulations; when rewarding troops in time of war, each province has fixed amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo memorialized, "An observation commissioner holds Your Majesty's territory in trust and proclaims Your Majesty's statutes. Rewards to troops on campaign are fixed by regulation for each province.

sentences.zh: 而士矩與奪由己，盈縮自專，不唯貽弊一方，必致諸軍援例。

translations.literal: Yet Shiju gave and took at his own discretion, controlling surplus and deficit by himself; this not only brings harm to one region—it will certainly cause all armies to cite his example.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shiju has distributed and withheld funds at his own pleasure, controlling surpluses and shortfalls as he sees fit. This will not only corrupt one region—it will invite every army in the empire to follow his example.

sentences.zh: 請下法司，正行朝典。」

translations.literal: I request that the matter be sent to the judicial offices and the court statutes properly enforced.」
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the case be referred to the judicial authorities and punished according to statute."

sentences.zh: 士矩坐貶蔡州別駕。

translations.literal: Shiju was convicted and demoted to Vice Prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiju was found guilty and demoted to Vice Prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 兼謨尋轉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Jian Mo soon transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo was soon transferred to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，檢校工部尚書、太原尹，充河東節度使。

translations.literal: The next year he served as acting Minister of Works and Governor of Taiyuan, and was appointed military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made acting Minister of Works and Governor of Taiyuan, with the additional title of Military Governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，累歴方鎮，卒。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he successively served in frontier commands and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang reign he served in several frontier commands in succession and then died.

sentences.zh: 王方慶，雍州咸陽人也，周少司空石泉公褒之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Fangqing—Wang Fangqing was a native of Xianyang in Yong Province and the great-grandson of Bao, Duke of Shiquan and Junior Minister of Works under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fangqing was a native of Xianyang in Yong Province and the great-grandson of Bao, Duke of Shiquan and former Junior Minister of Works under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 其先自琅邪南度，居於丹陽，爲江左冠族。

translations.literal: His ancestors crossed south from Langye and settled at Danyang, becoming an eminent clan of the Jiangzuo region.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had migrated south from Langye and settled at Danyang, where they became one of the great families of the Jiangzuo region.

sentences.zh: 褒北徙入關，始家咸陽焉。

translations.literal: Bao moved north into the Pass and first established the family at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao moved north through the Pass and first established the family seat at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 祖鼒，隋衞尉丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zi was Deputy Director of the Palace Guard under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zi served the Sui as Deputy Director of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 伯父弘讓，有美名，貞觀中爲中書舍人。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Hongrang had a fine reputation and served in the Zhenguan era as Drafting Officer of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Hongrang enjoyed a fine reputation and served during the Zhenguan reign as Drafting Officer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父弘直，爲漢王元昌友，畋獵無度，乃上書切諫，其略曰：「夫宗子維城之托者，所以固邦家之業也。

translations.literal: His father Hongzhi was friend to Prince Yuan Chang of Han; the prince hunted without measure, and Hongzhi submitted an urgent memorial, the gist of which was: 「The trust placed in imperial sons as city walls is meant to secure the enterprise of state and family.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongzhi served as companion to Prince Yuan Chang of Han. The prince hunted without restraint, and Hongzhi submitted a forceful memorial, which in essence said, "Imperial sons are entrusted as the walls of the realm precisely so that the fortunes of state and dynasty may be secured.

sentences.zh: 大王功無任城戰克之效，行無河間樂善之譽，爵高五等，邑富千室，當思答極施之洪慈，保無疆之永祚。

translations.literal: Great Prince, your merit lacks the effect of Rencheng's battle victories, and your conduct lacks the reputation of Hejian's delight in good deeds; your rank is of the fifth grade and your fief rich with a thousand households—you should think to repay the utmost grace shown you and preserve boundless eternal fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has won no victories like those of the Prince of Rencheng, nor earned a name for virtue like the Prince of Hejian, yet your rank stands among the highest and your fief holds a thousand households. You ought to repay the boundless grace shown you and safeguard an inheritance without end.

sentences.zh: 其爲計者，在乎修德，冠屨《詩》《禮》，畋獵史傳。

translations.literal: The plan for this lies in cultivating virtue: let cap and shoes be found in the Classic of Poetry and the Rites, and let hunting be found in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: The proper course is to cultivate virtue—let your cap and shoes be guided by the Classic of Poetry and the Rites, and let your hunting be measured by the lessons of history.

sentences.zh: 覽古人成敗之所由，鑒既往存亡之異跡，覆前戒後，居安慮危。

translations.literal: Survey the causes of success and failure among the ancients, mirror the different traces of survival and extinction in what has passed, overturn what lies before to warn what comes after, and in peace consider peril.
translations.idiomatic: Study why the ancients rose or fell, weigh the divergent fates of those who came before, take past errors as warnings for the future, and in security keep peril in mind.

sentences.zh: 奈何列騎齊驅，交橫壟畝，野有遊客，巷無居人。

translations.literal: How then can you array horses to gallop together, crossing and recrossing the fields, so that the countryside has only wanderers and the lanes have no residents?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you ride out with columns of horses thundering across the fields until the countryside is emptied of farmers and the lanes stand deserted.

sentences.zh: 貽眾庶之憂，逞一情之樂，從禽不息，實用寒心。」

translations.literal: You bequeath worry to the common multitude, indulge the pleasure of a single whim, and follow the chase without cease—this truly makes the heart grow cold.」
translations.idiomatic: You burden the people with fear, indulge a private pleasure, and hunt without end. It is enough to chill the heart."

sentences.zh: 元昌覽書而遽止。

translations.literal: Yuan Chang read the letter and immediately stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chang read the memorial and at once gave up the hunt.

sentences.zh: 漸見疏斥，轉荊王友。

translations.literal: Hongzhi gradually came to be seen as estranged and was transferred to serve as friend to the Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi gradually fell out of favor and was transferred to serve as companion to the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Longshuo era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Longshuo reign.

sentences.zh: 方慶年十六，起家越王府參軍。

translations.literal: Fangqing at age sixteen began his career as military adjutant in the household of the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing entered service at sixteen as military adjutant in the household of the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 嘗就記室任希古受《史記》、《漢書》。

translations.literal: He once studied the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han under the recorder Ren Xigu.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han under the prince's recorder, Ren Xigu.

sentences.zh: 希古遷爲太子舍人，方慶隨之卒業。

translations.literal: When Xigu was transferred to be aide to the crown prince, Fangqing followed him and completed his studies.
translations.idiomatic: When Xigu was transferred to serve as aide to the crown prince, Fangqing followed him and finished his course of study.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，累遷太仆少卿。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era he was promoted to Deputy Master of Horse.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchun reign he rose to Deputy Master of Horse.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，拜廣州都督。

translations.literal: When Empress Zetian held court, he was appointed Protector-General of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed the throne, he was appointed Protector-General of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣州地際南海，每歳有昆侖乘舶以珍物與中國交市。

translations.literal: Guangzhou borders the South Sea, and each year Kunlun people came by ship with precious goods to trade with China.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou lay on the South Sea, and every year Kunlun merchants arrived by ship bearing precious goods to trade with the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 舊都督路元睿冒求其貨，昆侖懷刃殺之。

translations.literal: The former Protector-General Lu Yuanrui boldly sought their goods, and the Kunlun concealed blades and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The previous Protector-General, Lu Yuanrui, had brazenly extorted their merchandise, and the Kunlun merchants, blades hidden on their persons, killed him.

sentences.zh: 方慶在任數載，秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Fangqing was in office several years and did not violate so much as an autumn hair.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing held the post for several years without taking so much as a hair's worth of improper gain.

sentences.zh: 又管內諸州首領，舊多貪縱，百姓有詣府稱冤者，府官以先受首領參餉，未嘗鞫問。

translations.literal: Moreover, the tribal chiefs of the various prefectures within his jurisdiction had formerly been mostly greedy and unrestrained; when commoners came to the office to cry injustice, the office officials, because they had already received tribute gifts from the chiefs, never examined the cases.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs of the prefectures under his jurisdiction had long been greedy and lawless. When commoners came to the prefectural office to plead injustice, the staff never investigated, having already accepted gifts from those same chiefs.

sentences.zh: 方慶乃集止府僚，絶其交往，首領縱暴者悉繩之，由是境內清肅。

translations.literal: Fangqing then assembled and restrained the staff officials, cut off their dealings with the chiefs, and bound by law all chiefs who were violent; thereby the territory within his jurisdiction became clear and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing summoned his staff, forbade such dealings, and punished every chief who abused his power. Thereafter the region was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 當時議者以爲有唐以來，治廣州者無出方慶之右。

translations.literal: Commentators of the time thought that since the Tang began, none who governed Guangzhou surpassed Fangqing.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held that since the founding of Tang, no governor of Guangzhou had matched Fangqing.

sentences.zh: 有制褒之曰：「朕以卿歴職著稱，故授此官，既美化遠聞，實副朝寄。

translations.literal: An imperial decree praised him, saying: 「We, because you have been noted in successive posts, therefore gave you this office; now that your beautifying governance is heard from afar, you have truly fulfilled the court's entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial decree praised him, saying, "We appointed you to this post because of your distinguished record in office. Your governance has now won renown far and wide and has truly fulfilled the trust the court placed in you.

sentences.zh: 令賜卿雜采六十段，並瑞錦等物，以彰善政也。」

translations.literal: We order that you be given sixty bolts of mixed silks, together with auspicious brocades and other goods, to manifest good governance."
translations.idiomatic: We therefore grant you sixty bolts of assorted silks, together with auspicious brocades and other gifts, in recognition of your excellent administration."

sentences.zh: 證聖元年，召拜洛州長史，尋加銀青光祿大夫，封石泉縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengsheng he was summoned and appointed Chief Secretary of Luozhou; soon he was given the title Silver Azure Glory Grand Master of Imperial Secretariat and enfeoffed as Baron of Shiquan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengsheng he was summoned as Chief Secretary of Luozhou; shortly afterward he was granted the title Silver Azure Glory Grand Master of Imperial Secretariat and ennobled as Baron of Shiquan County.

sentences.zh: 萬歳登封元年，轉并州長史，封琅邪縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wansui Dengfeng he transferred to Chief Secretary of Bingzhou and was enfeoffed as Baron of Langye County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wansui Dengfeng reign he was transferred to Chief Secretary of Bingzhou and ennobled as Baron of Langye County.

sentences.zh: 未行，遷鸞臺侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Luantai and Associate Grand Counselor of Fengge and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the Bingzhou post, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Luantai and appointed Associate Grand Counselor of Fengge and Luantai.

sentences.zh: 俄轉鳳閣侍郎，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he transferred to Vice Minister of Fengge and, as before, managed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Vice Minister of Fengge and continued to participate in governing as before.

sentences.zh: 神功元年七月，清邊道大總管建安王攸宜破契丹凱還，欲以是月詣闕獻俘。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Shenggong, Youyi, Prince of Ji'an and Commander-in-Chief of the Qingbian Circuit, defeated the Khitans and returned in triumph, wishing to go to court that month to present captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Shenggong, Prince Youyi of Ji'an, Commander-in-Chief of the Qingbian Circuit, defeated the Khitans and returned in triumph, intending to present captives at court that same month.

sentences.zh: 內史王及善以爲將軍入城，例有軍樂，既今上孝明高皇帝忌月，請備而不奏。

translations.literal: The Imperial Secretary Wang Jishan thought that when a general enters the city there is by precedent military music, but since it was the mourning month of the present sovereign's Xiao Ming High Emperor, he requested that the music be prepared but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Secretary Wang Jishan noted that a victorious general entering the capital was normally greeted with military music, but as the month fell within the mourning period for Emperor Gaozong, he proposed that the instruments be prepared but not played.

sentences.zh: 方慶奏曰：「臣按禮經，但有忌日，而無忌月。

translations.literal: Fangqing memorialized: 「Your subject has examined the ritual classics and finds that there are mourning days, but no mourning months.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing memorialized, "Your subject has consulted the ritual classics and finds that mourning is observed on anniversaries of death, but not throughout entire months.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝納後，用九月九日，是康帝忌月，於時持疑不定。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mu of Jin took an empress, the date chosen was the ninth day of the ninth month, which was Emperor Kang's mourning month; at the time opinion was held in doubt and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mu of Jin took an empress on the ninth day of the ninth month—the mourning month of Emperor Kang—the court was uncertain what to do.

sentences.zh: 下太常，禮官荀訥議稱：『禮隻有忌日，無忌月。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the ritual official Xun Ne argued: 『In ritual there are only mourning days, not mourning months.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, where the ritual specialist Xun Ne argued, 'The rites prescribe mourning days, not mourning months."

sentences.zh: 若有忌月，即有忌時、忌歳，益無理據。』

translations.literal: If there were mourning months, then there would also be mourning seasons and mourning years—there is increasingly no rational basis for this.』
translations.idiomatic: If one admitted mourning months, one would have to admit mourning seasons and mourning years as well, which has no basis in reason.

sentences.zh: 當時從訥所議。

translations.literal: At the time the court followed Ne's argument.
translations.idiomatic: The court at the time accepted Xun Ne's view.

sentences.zh: 軍樂是軍容，與常不等，臣謂振作於事無嫌。」

translations.literal: Military music is a matter of military bearing and is not the same as ordinary music; your subject holds that performing it in this matter would be without offense.」
translations.idiomatic: Military music belongs to the display of martial ceremony and is not ordinary festivity. Your subject believes that performing it on this occasion would give no cause for offense."

sentences.zh: 則天從之。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 則天嘗幸萬安山玉泉寺，以山逕危懸，欲禦腰輿而上。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian once visited Yuquan Temple on Mount Wan'an; because the mountain path was perilously suspended, she wished to ride a waist litter up.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once visited Yuquan Temple on Mount Wan'an. Because the mountain path was steep and treacherous, she intended to be carried up in a waist litter.

sentences.zh: 方慶諫曰：「昔漢元帝嘗祭廟，出便門，禦樓船，光祿勳張猛奏曰：『乘船危，就橋安。』

translations.literal: Fangqing remonstrated: 「Formerly Emperor Yuan of Han once sacrificed at the ancestral temple, exited Bian Gate, and rode a tower boat; the Director of Imperial Parks Zhang Meng memorialized: 『Riding a boat is dangerous; taking the bridge is safe.』
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing remonstrated, "In the past Emperor Yuan of Han, leaving to perform temple sacrifice through Bian Gate, boarded a tower boat. Zhang Meng, Director of Imperial Parks, memorialized, 'Going by boat is perilous; going by bridge is safe.

sentences.zh: 元帝乃從橋，即前代舊事。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan then took the bridge—this is a precedent from former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan then took the bridge—a precedent from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今山徑危險，石路曲狹，上瞻駭目，下視寒心，比於樓船，安危不等。

translations.literal: Now the mountain path is dangerous, the stone road winding and narrow; looking up startles the eyes, looking down chills the heart—compared with a tower boat, safety and danger are not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Today's mountain path is far more dangerous: the stone track is narrow and twisting, dreadful to look up at and chilling to look down from. Compared with a tower boat, the difference in risk is not slight.

sentences.zh: 陛下蒸人父母，奈何踐此畏塗？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is parent to the common people—how can you tread this fearful path?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is father and mother to the people—how can you set foot on so fearful a path?

sentences.zh: 伏望停輿駐蹕。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will halt the carriage and halt your progress.」
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that Your Majesty halt the carriage and go no farther.'"

sentences.zh: 則天納其言而止。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian accepted his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu accepted his counsel and abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 是歳，改封石泉子。

translations.literal: That year his enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Shiquan.
translations.idiomatic: That year his title was raised to Viscount of Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 時有制，每月一日於明堂行告朔之禮。

translations.literal: At the time there was a regulation that on the first day of each month the first-of-month ritual was performed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a regulation required that on the first day of each month the gaoshuo rite be performed in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 司禮博士辟閭仁諝奏議，其略曰：「經史正文，無天子每月告朔之事，唯《禮記·玉藻》云：『天子聽朔於南門之外。』

translations.literal: The Director of Ritual Studies Pimilu Renxu submitted a memorial for discussion, the gist of which was: 「In the proper texts of the classics and histories there is no matter of the Son of Heaven performing the monthly gaoshuo ritual; only the Jade Regalia chapter of the Book of Rites says: 『The Son of Heaven hears the first-of-month announcement outside the south gate.』
translations.idiomatic: Pimilu Renxu, Director of Ritual Studies, submitted a memorial for discussion, which in essence said, "The canonical texts of the classics and histories contain no instance of the Son of Heaven performing a monthly gaoshuo rite. Only the Jade Regalia chapter of the Book of Rites states, 'The Son of Heaven receives the first-of-month announcement outside the south gate.

sentences.zh: 其每月告朔者，諸侯之禮也。

translations.literal: The monthly gaoshuo ritual is the rite of feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The monthly gaoshuo rite, however, is the ceremony of feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按《禮論》及《三禮義宗》、《江都集禮》、《貞觀禮》、《顯慶禮》及《祠令》，無天子每月告朔之事。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully examined the Discussions of Rites, the Compendium of the Meanings of the Three Rites, the Jiangdu Collected Rites, the Zhenguan Rites, the Xianqing Rites, and the Sacrifice Regulations, and found no matter of the Son of Heaven performing the monthly gaoshuo ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has carefully consulted the Discussions of Rites, the Compendium of the Meanings of the Three Rites, the Jiangdu Collected Rites, the Zhenguan Rites, the Xianqing Rites, and the Sacrifice Regulations, and finds in none of them any provision for a monthly gaoshuo rite performed by the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 若以爲無明堂故無告朔之禮，有明堂即合告朔，則周、秦有明堂而無天子每月告朔之事。

translations.literal: If one thinks that because there was no Bright Hall there was no gaoshuo ritual, and that having a Bright Hall means gaoshuo should be performed, then Zhou and Qin had Bright Halls yet had no matter of the Son of Heaven performing the monthly gaoshuo ritual.
translations.idiomatic: If the argument is that the rite is absent only because there is no Bright Hall, and that possessing a Bright Hall necessarily entails gaoshuo, then the Zhou and Qin dynasties both had Bright Halls—yet nowhere is there record of the Son of Heaven performing a monthly gaoshuo rite.

sentences.zh: 臣等參求，既無其禮，不可習非，以天子之尊而用諸侯之禮。」

translations.literal: Your subjects have examined and sought it; since there is no such ritual, one must not learn what is wrong, using feudal lords' rites with the Son of Heaven's exalted dignity."
translations.idiomatic: We have investigated the matter thoroughly: no such rite exists in the records, and we must not adopt a false precedent by imposing a feudal lord's ceremony upon the Son of Heaven.'"

sentences.zh: 方慶又奏議，其略曰：「明堂，天子布政之宮也。

translations.literal: Fang Qing again submitted a memorial for discussion, the gist of which was: "The Bright Hall is the palace where the Son of Heaven promulgates government.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qing submitted his own memorial for discussion, which in essence stated, "The Bright Hall is where the Son of Heaven promulgates government.

sentences.zh: 謹按《穀梁傳》云：『閏者，附月之餘日，天子不以告朔。』

translations.literal: Respectfully I examine the Guliang Commentary, which says: "An intercalary month is the surplus days attached to a month; the Son of Heaven does not perform gaoshuo for it.
translations.idiomatic: I have carefully consulted the Guliang Commentary, which states, "An intercalary month consists of surplus days attached to the preceding month; the Son of Heaven does not perform gaoshuo on such a month."

sentences.zh: 『非禮也。

translations.literal: It is not according to rite.
translations.idiomatic: That is not in accordance with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 閏以正時，時以作事，事以厚生，生人之道，於是乎在矣。

translations.literal: Intercalation is to correct the seasons; seasons are to undertake affairs; affairs are to enrich life—the Way of sustaining humanity lies herein.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalation adjusts the seasons; the seasons govern human activity; activity sustains life. In this lies the whole way of nourishing the people.

sentences.zh: 不告閏朔，棄時政也。』

translations.literal: Not announcing the intercalary first-of-month is to abandon governance according to the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: To fail to announce the intercalary month's new moon is to abandon seasonal governance altogether.

sentences.zh: 臣據此文，則天子閏月亦告朔矣。

translations.literal: According to this passage, the Son of Heaven also performs gaoshuo in an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: From this passage it follows that the Son of Heaven ought to perform gaoshuo even in an intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 寧有他月而廢其禮乎？

translations.literal: How could other months have the rite abolished?
translations.idiomatic: Would he observe the rite in one month and abandon it in another?

sentences.zh: 先儒舊説，天子行事，一年十八度入明堂矣。

translations.literal: According to the old teachings of earlier scholars, in the Son of Heaven's activities, in one year he enters the Bright Hall eighteen times.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars held that in the course of a year the Son of Heaven entered the Bright Hall on eighteen separate occasions.

sentences.zh: 大享不問卜，一入也；

translations.literal: Great sacrifices without divination—one entry;
translations.idiomatic: One entry for the great sacrifice without divination;

sentences.zh: 每月告朔，十二入也；

translations.literal: monthly gaoshuo—twelve entries;
translations.idiomatic: twelve entries for the monthly gaoshuo rite;

sentences.zh: 四時迎氣，四入也；

translations.literal: receiving qi in the four seasons—four entries;
translations.idiomatic: four entries for receiving the seasonal qi;

sentences.zh: 巡狩之年，一入也。

translations.literal: in years of imperial tour—one entry.
translations.idiomatic: and one entry in years of the imperial tour.

sentences.zh: 今禮官議唯歳首一入耳，與先儒既異，在臣不敢同。

translations.literal: Now the ritual officials propose only one entry at the year's beginning, which already differs from earlier scholars; your subject dares not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials now propose only a single annual entry at the year's beginning—a view already at odds with earlier scholarship, and one your subject cannot accept.

sentences.zh: 宋朝何承天纂集其文，以爲《禮論》，雖加編次，事則闕如。

translations.literal: In the Song dynasty He Chengtian compiled the texts into the Discussions of Rites; though he arranged them, the matter remains deficient.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liu Song dynasty He Chengtian gathered these texts into the Discussions of Rites, but although he put them in order, the subject itself remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 梁代崔靈恩撰《三禮義宗》，但捃摭前儒，因循故事而已。

translations.literal: In the Liang dynasty Cui Lin'en wrote the Compendium of the Meanings of the Three Rites, but only gathered earlier scholars and followed old precedents, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liang dynasty Cui Lin'en composed the Compendium of the Meanings of the Three Rites, yet he merely collected earlier scholars and repeated established precedent.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝命學士撰《江都集禮》，隻抄撮舊禮，更無異文。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui ordered scholars to compile the Jiangdu Collected Rites, merely copying and excerpting old rites, with no novel text whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui had scholars compile the Jiangdu Collected Rites, but they only copied older ritual texts and added nothing new.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀》、《顯慶禮》及《祠令》不言告朔者，蓋爲歴代不傳，所以其文乃闕。

translations.literal: That the Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and Sacrifice Regulations do not mention gaoshuo is probably because it was not transmitted through the ages, hence their texts are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and Sacrifice Regulations make no mention of gaoshuo because the practice had fallen out of transmission over the centuries, leaving those texts silent on the point.

sentences.zh: 各有緣由，不足依據。

translations.literal: Each has its reasons and is insufficient as a basis.
translations.idiomatic: Each omission has its own explanation, and none of these works can serve as reliable authority.

sentences.zh: 今禮官引爲明證，在臣誠實有疑。」

translations.literal: Now the ritual officials cite them as clear proof—in your subject's sincerity there are doubts."
translations.idiomatic: That the ritual officials now cite them as decisive proof is something your subject genuinely finds doubtful."

sentences.zh: 則天又令春官廣集眾儒，取方慶、仁諝所奏議，以定得失。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian then ordered the Ministry of Rites broadly to gather the multitude of scholars, taking the submitted memorials of Fang Qing and Renxu to determine what was right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian then ordered the Ministry of Rites to assemble a broad council of scholars and weigh the memorials submitted by Fang Qing and Renxu to settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 時成均博士吳揚善、太學博士郭山惲等奏：「按《周禮》及《三傳》，皆有天子告朔之禮，秦滅《詩》、《書》，由是告朔禮廢。

translations.literal: At the time the Director of the Imperial Academy Wu Yangshan, the Director of the Directorate of Education Guo Shanyun, and others memorialized: "According to the Rites of Zhou and the Three Commentaries, all contain the Son of Heaven's gaoshuo ritual; Qin destroyed the Odes and Documents, and thereby the gaoshuo ritual was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Yangshan, Director of the Imperial Academy, Guo Shanyun, Director of the Directorate of Education, and others submitted a memorial: "The Rites of Zhou and the Three Commentaries all attest to a gaoshuo rite performed by the Son of Heaven. When Qin destroyed the Odes and Documents, that rite fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 望依方慶議。」

translations.literal: We hope to follow Fang Qing's proposal."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Fang Qing's proposal be adopted."

sentences.zh: 有制從之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered compliance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the proposal be followed.

sentences.zh: 則天以方慶家多書籍，嘗訪求右軍遺跡。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian, because Fang Qing's family possessed many books, once sought surviving traces of the Right General.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fang Qing's household held an extensive library, Empress Zetian once asked him to search out surviving works of the Right General, Wang Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 方慶奏曰：「臣十代從伯祖羲之書，先有四十餘紙，貞觀十二年，太宗購求，先臣並已進之。

translations.literal: Fang Qing memorialized, saying: "Your subject originally had more than forty sheets of calligraphy by my tenth-generation elder cousin Wang Xizhi; in the twelfth year of Zhenguan, Emperor Taizong sought to purchase them, and my predecessors all presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qing replied in a memorial: "Your subject once possessed more than forty sheets of calligraphy by my tenth-generation elder cousin Wang Xizhi. In the twelfth year of the Zhenguan era Emperor Taizong sought to acquire them, and my forebears had already presented them all.

sentences.zh: 唯有一卷見今在。

translations.literal: Only one scroll remains in possession today.
translations.idiomatic: Only one scroll remains in my possession today.

sentences.zh: 又進臣十一代祖導、十代祖洽、九代祖珣、八代祖曇首、七代祖僧綽、六代祖仲寶、五代祖騫、高祖規、曾祖褒，並九代三從伯祖晉中書令獻之已下二十八人書，共十卷。」

translations.literal: I also present calligraphy by my eleventh-generation ancestor Dao, tenth-generation ancestor Qia, ninth-generation ancestor Xun, eighth-generation ancestor Tanshou, seventh-generation ancestor Sengchuo, sixth-generation ancestor Zhongbao, fifth-generation ancestor Qian, great-grandfather Gui, great-great-grandfather Bao, together with my ninth-generation thrice-removed elder cousin Jin Secretariat Director Xianzhi and twenty-eight others below him, ten scrolls in all."
translations.idiomatic: I also present calligraphy by my eleventh-generation ancestor Wang Dao, tenth-generation ancestor Wang Qia, ninth-generation ancestor Wang Xun, eighth-generation ancestor Wang Tanshou, seventh-generation ancestor Wang Sengchuo, sixth-generation ancestor Wang Zhongbao, fifth-generation ancestor Wang Qian, my great-grandfather Wang Gui, my great-great-grandfather Wang Bao, and, together with my ninth-generation thrice-removed elder cousin Wang Xianzhi, former Director of the Secretariat under the Jin, and twenty-eight others of the family below him—ten scrolls in all."

sentences.zh: 則天禦武成殿示群臣，仍令中書舍人崔融爲《寶章集》，以敘其事，復賜方慶，當時甚以爲榮。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian went to Wucheng Hall to show the officials, and ordered Drafting Secretary Cui Rong to compose the Precious Scrolls Collection to narrate the affair, again bestowing it upon Fang Qing; at the time it was greatly regarded as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian then received the court in Wucheng Hall and displayed the works to her ministers. She ordered Drafting Secretary Cui Rong to compose the Precious Scrolls Collection narrating the event, and bestowed the collection again upon Fang Qing—a distinction widely regarded at the time as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 方慶又舉：「令杖『期喪、大功未葬，不預朝賀；

translations.literal: Fang Qing also proposed: "I invoke the regulation: "Those in first-year mourning or second-degree mourning before burial shall not participate in court congratulations;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qing also submitted a proposal citing the regulation: "Those observing first-year mourning or second-degree mourning before burial shall not attend court congratulations;

sentences.zh: 未終喪，不預宴會。』

translations.literal: before mourning is complete, one shall not participate in banquets.
translations.idiomatic: and before mourning is complete, one shall not attend banquets.

sentences.zh: 比來朝官不遵禮法，身有哀容，陪預朝會，手舞足蹈，公違憲章，名教既虧，實玷皇化。

translations.literal: Recently court officials have not observed ritual law; bearing mournful countenance, they attend and participate in court assemblies, clapping hands and dancing—openly violating statutes, moral teaching already impaired, truly tarnishing imperial transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet of late many court officials have ignored these rules, appearing at assemblies with faces still marked by grief yet clapping and dancing along with the rest—open defiance of statute, an erosion of moral teaching, and a real stain upon the court's example.

sentences.zh: 伏望申明令式，更禁斷。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope the regulations may be clarified and further forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that the regulations be restated clearly and the practice forbidden once again."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was accepted.

sentences.zh: 方慶漸以老疾，乞從閑逸，乃授麟臺監修國史。

translations.literal: Fang Qing, gradually afflicted by age and illness, requested leisurely retirement and was appointed Director of the Imperial Library with charge over compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: As age and illness gradually overtook him, Fang Qing asked to be released to a quieter post and was appointed Director of the Imperial Library with responsibility for compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 及中宗立爲東宮，方慶兼檢校太子左庶子。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was established as Eastern Palace Heir, Fang Qing was concurrently made Acting Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was named Heir Apparent, Fang Qing was concurrently appointed Acting Left Assistant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 聖曆二年一日，則天欲季冬講武，有司稽緩，延入孟春。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second year of Shengli, Empress Zetian wished to conduct martial exercises in late winter; the responsible officials delayed matters, postponing it into early spring.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the second year of the Shengli era, Empress Zetian planned to hold martial exercises in late winter, but the responsible offices moved slowly and the event was postponed into early spring.

sentences.zh: 方慶上疏曰：「謹按《禮記月令》：『孟冬之月，天子命將帥講武，習射禦角力。』

translations.literal: Fang Qing submitted a memorial, saying: "Respectfully I examine the Monthly Ordinances in the Book of Rites: "In the month of early winter, the Son of Heaven orders generals and commanders to conduct martial exercises, practicing archery and controlling strength contests.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qing submitted a memorial: "I have carefully consulted the Monthly Ordinances in the Book of Rites, which state, 'In the month of early winter the Son of Heaven orders his generals to conduct martial exercises, practicing archery and testing strength in combat.'

sentences.zh: 此乃三時務農，一時講武，以習射禦，角校才力，蓋王者常事，安不忘危之道也。

translations.literal: This is three seasons devoted to agriculture, one season to martial exercises—to practice archery and charioteering, compare strength and talent; it is the constant business of a king, the way of security without forgetting danger.
translations.idiomatic: This reflects the principle that three seasons are given to farming and one to military training—to practice archery and charioteering and test men's strength and skill. Such exercises are the constant duty of a ruler, the way of remaining secure without forgetting danger.

sentences.zh: 『孟春之月，不可以稱兵。』

translations.literal: In the month of early spring, one must not mobilize arms.
translations.idiomatic: The text also says, 'In the month of early spring one must not mobilize arms.'

sentences.zh: 兵者，甲胄干戈之總名。

translations.literal: Arms are the general term for armor, helmets, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Arms are the general name for armor, helmets, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 兵金性，克木，春盛德在木，而舉金以害盛德，逆生氣。

translations.literal: Arms have the nature of metal, which overcomes wood; in spring the flourishing virtue resides in wood, yet raising metal to harm the flourishing virtue reverses the generative qi.
translations.idiomatic: Arms belong to the element metal, which overcomes wood. In spring the flourishing virtue resides in wood, so to raise metal against it is to violate the generative qi of the season.

sentences.zh: 『孟春行冬令，則水潦爲敗，雪霜大摯，首種不入。』

translations.literal: If in early spring one executes winter ordinances, then floods become ruinous, frost and snow fall heavily, and the first sowing cannot take root."
translations.idiomatic: It further warns, 'If winter ordinances are enforced in early spring, floods will bring ruin, frost and snow will fall heavily, and the first sowing will fail to take root.'

sentences.zh: 蔡邕《月令章句》云：『太陰新休，少陽尚微，而行冬令以導水氣，故水潦至而敗生物也。

translations.literal: Cai Yong's Commentary on the Monthly Ordinances states: "The great yin has newly rested, the lesser yang is still slight, yet executing winter ordinances to channel water qi causes floods to arrive and ruin living things.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's Commentary on the Monthly Ordinances explains, 'The great yin has only just withdrawn and the lesser yang is still weak; to enforce winter ordinances then is to summon water qi, so floods come and destroy living things.

sentences.zh: 雪霜大摯，折陽者也。

translations.literal: Heavy frost and snow breaks the yang.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy frost and snow break the yang force of the season.

sentences.zh: 太陰幹時，雨雪而霜，故大傷首種。

translations.literal: The great yin dominates the season, rain and snow turn to frost, hence greatly harming the first sowing.
translations.idiomatic: When the great yin dominates the season, rain and snow turn to frost and the first sowing suffers severe harm.

sentences.zh: 首種，謂宿麥也，麥以秋種，故謂之首種。

translations.literal: First sowing means winter wheat; wheat is sown in autumn, hence it is called first sowing.
translations.idiomatic: The first sowing refers to winter wheat, sown in autumn and therefore called the first crop of the year.

sentences.zh: 入，收也，春爲沍寒所傷，故至夏麥不成長也。』

translations.literal: "Ru" means to harvest; spring harmed by severe cold, so by summer the wheat cannot mature.
translations.idiomatic: The word "ru" here means to ripen for harvest: harmed by the bitter cold of spring, the wheat cannot mature by summer.'

sentences.zh: 今孟春講武，是行冬令，以陰政犯陽氣，害發生之德。

translations.literal: Conducting martial exercises now in early spring is to execute winter ordinances, using yin governance to violate yang qi, harming the virtue of generation.
translations.idiomatic: To conduct martial exercises now, in early spring, is to enforce winter ordinances—to let yin governance violate yang qi and injure the virtue of generation itself.

sentences.zh: 臣恐水潦敗物，霜雪損稼，夏麥不登，無所收入也。

translations.literal: Your subject fears floods ruining things, frost and snow damaging crops, summer wheat failing to ripen, and nothing to harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject fears floods will destroy the crops, frost and snow will ruin the fields, the summer wheat will fail to ripen, and there will be nothing to harvest.

sentences.zh: 伏望天恩不違時令，至孟冬教習，以順天道。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Heaven's grace will not violate the seasonal ordinances, and that training be deferred until early winter, in accord with Heaven's Way."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty not violate the seasonal ordinances, and that the training be postponed until early winter in accord with Heaven's Way."

sentences.zh: 手製答曰：「比爲久屬太平，多歴年載，人皆廢戰，並悉學文。

translations.literal: The emperor personally replied: "Recently we have long belonged to great peace, for many years; all have abandoned warfare and entirely devoted themselves to letters.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress replied in her own hand: "We have enjoyed peace for many years now. People everywhere have laid aside warfare and turned wholly to learning.

sentences.zh: 今者用整兵威，故令教習。

translations.literal: Now we must restore military prestige, hence the order for training.
translations.idiomatic: It is now necessary to restore military discipline, which is why training has been ordered.

sentences.zh: 卿以春行冬令，則水潦爲敗，舉金傷木，則便害發生。

translations.literal: You say that spring executing winter ordinances brings floods as ruin, and raising metal to harm wood then injures generation.
translations.idiomatic: You argue that to enforce winter ordinances in spring brings floods, and that raising metal against wood injures the season's power of generation.

sentences.zh: 循覽所陳，深合典禮，若違此請，乃月令虛行。

translations.literal: Having reviewed what you set forth, it deeply accords with canonical rites; if this request were disregarded, the Monthly Ordinances would be hollow words.
translations.idiomatic: On reading what you have set forth, I find it deeply in accord with canonical ritual. To disregard this request would be to render the Monthly Ordinances meaningless.

sentences.zh: 佇啟直言，用依來表。」

translations.literal: I await your forthright counsel; your memorial shall be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Continue to speak plainly as you have done; your memorial will be followed."

sentences.zh: 是歳，正授太子左庶子，封石泉公，餘並如故，俸料同職事三品，兼侍皇太子讀書。

translations.literal: That year he was formally appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Shiquan, remaining duties as before, salary equal to active third rank, concurrently attending the Crown Prince in his studies.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fang Qing was formally appointed Left Assistant to the Crown Prince and enfeoffed as Duke of Shiquan. His other duties remained unchanged, his salary was set equal to that of an active third-rank official, and he was also charged with attending the Crown Prince in his studies.

sentences.zh: 方慶又上言：「謹按史籍所載，人臣與人主言及上表，未有稱皇太子名者。

translations.literal: Fang Qing again submitted, saying: "Respectfully examining what historical records contain, when ministers speak to the ruler or submit memorials, there has never been one who used the Crown Prince's personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qing submitted another memorial: "A careful review of the historical records shows that when ministers addressed the ruler or submitted memorials, none ever used the Crown Prince's personal name.

sentences.zh: 當爲太子皇儲，其名尊重，不敢指斥，所以不言。

translations.literal: As heir and royal reserve, his name is revered; one dares not point and call it, hence it is not spoken.
translations.idiomatic: As heir and royal reserve, his name is too exalted to be spoken directly; one dares not utter it, and therefore does not.

sentences.zh: 晉尚書僕射山濤啟事，稱皇太子而不言名。

translations.literal: Jin Vice Director of the Secretariat Shan Tao in his reports addressed the Crown Prince without naming him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin dynasty, Vice Director of the Secretariat Shan Tao addressed his reports to "the Crown Prince" without using the heir's name.

sentences.zh: 濤中朝名士，必詳典故，其不稱名，應有憑準。

translations.literal: Shan Tao was a renowned scholar of the central court, thoroughly versed in precedents; his not naming him must have had authoritative basis.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao was a leading scholar of the central court and thoroughly versed in precedent; his avoidance of the name must have rested on solid authority.

sentences.zh: 朝官尚猶如此，宮臣歸則不疑。

translations.literal: If court officials still observe this, palace officials would certainly have no doubts.
translations.idiomatic: If even court officials observed this rule, palace officials would surely have followed it without question.

sentences.zh: 今東宮殿及門名，皆有觸犯，臨事論啟，回避甚難。

translations.literal: Now the Eastern Palace halls and gate names all contain taboo violations; in daily business and memorials, avoiding them is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: At present the names of halls and gates in the Eastern Palace all contain characters that violate this taboo, making it very difficult to conduct business or draft memorials without offense.

sentences.zh: 孝敬皇帝爲太子時，改弘教門爲崇教門；

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaojing was Crown Prince, Hongjiao Gate was changed to Chongjiao Gate;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaojing was Crown Prince, Hongjiao Gate was renamed Chongjiao Gate;

sentences.zh: 沛王爲皇太子，改崇賢館爲崇文館。

translations.literal: when the Prince of Pei was Crown Prince, Chongxian Pavilion was changed to Chongwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: when the Prince of Pei was Crown Prince, Chongxian Pavilion was renamed Chongwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 皆避名諱，以遵典禮。

translations.literal: All avoided the taboo name to follow canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: Both changes avoided the heir's personal name in accordance with canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 此即成例，足爲軌模。

translations.literal: These already constitute precedent, sufficient as a model.
translations.idiomatic: These precedents are sufficient to serve as a model.

sentences.zh: 伏望天恩因循舊式，付司改換。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Heaven's grace will follow the old practice and charge the officials to change them."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty follow the established practice and order the responsible offices to make the changes."

sentences.zh: 製從之。

translations.literal: The imperial reply ordered compliance.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial reply ordered that the proposal be followed.

sentences.zh: 長安二年五月卒，贈袞州都督，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Chang'an he died; posthumously appointed Area Commander of Yanzhou, posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the second year of the Chang'an era. He was posthumously appointed Area Commander of Yanzhou and given the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以宮僚之舊，追贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, because of their old ties as palace staff, he was posthumously promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, he posthumously promoted Fang Qing to Minister of Personnel in recognition of their former service together in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 方慶博學好著述，所撰雜書凡二百餘卷。

translations.literal: Fang Qing was broadly learned and fond of writing; miscellaneous works he authored totaled more than two hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qing was broadly learned and devoted to writing; his miscellaneous works totaled more than two hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 尤精《三禮》，好事者多詢訪之。

translations.literal: He was especially expert in the Three Rites; many enthusiasts consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially expert in the Three Rites, and many scholars sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 每所酬答，鹹有典據，故時人編次，名曰《禮雜答問》。

translations.literal: Every answer he gave had canonical basis; therefore contemporaries compiled them under the title Miscellaneous Questions and Answers on Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Every answer he gave was grounded in canonical authority, and contemporaries compiled them under the title Miscellaneous Questions and Answers on Rites.

sentences.zh: 聚書甚多，不減秘閣，至於圖畫，亦多異本。

translations.literal: He collected many books, no fewer than the Secret Archives; as for paintings, he also had many rare copies.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed a library rivaling the Secret Archives, and his collection of paintings included many rare copies as well.

sentences.zh: 諸子莫能守其業，卒後尋亦散亡。

translations.literal: None of his sons could preserve his estate; soon after his death it all scattered and was lost.
translations.idiomatic: None of his sons proved able to preserve his estate, and soon after his death the collection was scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 長子光輔，開元中官至潞州刺史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guangfu, in the Kaiyuan era reached office as Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guangfu rose during the Kaiyuan era to the post of Prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 少子晙，工書知名，尤善琴棋，而性多嚴整，官至殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His youngest son Jun was renowned for calligraphy, especially skilled in zither and chess, yet by nature stern and precise; he reached the office of Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Jun was known for his calligraphy and was especially skilled at the zither and chess, though by nature he was stern and exacting; he rose to the office of Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 姚璹，字令璋，散騎常侍思廉之孫也。

translations.literal: Yao Shu—Yao Shu, styled Lingzhang, grandson of Palace Attendant Yao Siliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shu, whose courtesy name was Lingzhang, was the grandson of Palace Attendant Yao Siliang.

sentences.zh: 少孤，撫弟妹以友愛稱。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he raised his younger siblings and was known for brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at a young age, he raised his younger brother and sister and was known for his devoted affection toward them.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，有才辯。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in classics and histories, talented and eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read in the classics and histories and was gifted with talent and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 永徽中明經擢第。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he passed the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era he passed the Classics examination.

sentences.zh: 累補太子宮門郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Gate Gentleman of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively appointed Gate Gentleman of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 與司議郎孟利貞等奉令撰《瑤山玉彩》書，書成，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: With Drafting Secretary Meng Lizhen and others he was ordered to compile the Jade Brilliance of Mount Yao; when the work was complete, he was promoted to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Drafting Secretary Meng Lizhen and others, he was ordered to compile the Jade Brilliance of Mount Yao. When the work was finished, he was promoted to Secretary.

sentences.zh: 調露中，累遷至中書舍人，封吳興縣男。

translations.literal: In the Tiaolu era he was successively promoted to Drafting Secretary, enfeoffed as Baron of Wuxing County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiaolu era he was successively promoted to Drafting Secretary and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuxing County.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，遷夏官侍郎。

translations.literal: When Empress Zetian held court, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Zetian assumed power, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 坐從父弟敬節同徐敬業之亂，貶桂州都督府長史。

translations.literal: Implicated because his father's younger cousin brother Jingjie joined Xu Jingye's rebellion, he was demoted to Senior Administrator of the Guizhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father's younger cousin Jingjie had joined Xu Jingye's rebellion, he was demoted to Senior Administrator of the Guizhou metropolitan government.

sentences.zh: 時則天雅好符瑞，璹至嶺南，訪諸山川草樹，其名號有「武」字者，皆以爲上膺國姓，列奏其事。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Zetian greatly favored portents; when Shu reached Lingnan, he investigated mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees whose names contained the character "Wu," all deeming them proof the ruler bore the national surname, and listed memorializing each instance.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian was then greatly fond of auspicious portents. When Shu reached Lingnan, he searched out mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees whose names contained the character "Wu," treating each as proof that the ruler embodied the dynastic surname, and memorialized them one by one.

sentences.zh: 則天大悅，召拜天官侍郎。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian was greatly pleased and summoned him to appointment as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian was greatly pleased and recalled him to appointment as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 善於選補，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Skilled at selection and appointment, contemporaries praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at selecting and appointing officials, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，遷文昌左丞、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-equal with the Empress's Secretariat as Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Changshou era he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and appointed Co-Grand Counselor of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 自永徽以後，左、右史雖得對仗承旨，仗下後謀議，皆不預聞。

translations.literal: Since Yonghui, although Left and Right Historians could respond in formal session to imperial intent, after dismissal of the court session they were not privy to deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yonghui era, although the Left and Right Historians could receive the emperor's intent during formal court sessions, they were not privy to deliberations held after the session adjourned.

sentences.zh: 璹以爲帝王謨訓，不可暫無紀述，若不宣自宰相，史官無從得書。

translations.literal: Shu believed imperial counsel and instruction could not go even briefly without record; if not announced through the chief counselor, historiographers had no means to write it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu argued that the counsel and instructions of the ruler could not go even briefly unrecorded: if they were not communicated through the chief counselor, the historiographers had no way to set them down.

sentences.zh: 乃表請仗下所言軍國政要，宰相一人專知撰錄，號爲時政記，每月封送史館。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized requesting that crucial military and civil affairs spoken after court session be recorded exclusively by one chief counselor, called the Record of Current Governance, sealed monthly and sent to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial requesting that important military and civil matters discussed after court sessions be recorded by a single chief counselor, under the title Record of Current Governance, sealed each month and forwarded to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 宰相之撰時政記，自璹始也。

translations.literal: Chief counselors' composition of the Record of Current Governance began with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of chief counselors compiling the Record of Current Governance began with Yao Shu.

sentences.zh: 是歳九月，坐事轉司賓少卿，罷知政事。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month, implicated in an offense he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Guests and dismissed from governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the ninth month, implicated in an offense, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Guests and removed from participation in government.

sentences.zh: 延載初，擢拜納言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanzai he was elevated and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yanzai era he was elevated to the post of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 有司以璹從父弟犯法，奏言不合更爲侍臣。

translations.literal: The responsible officials, because Shu's father's younger cousin brother violated the law, memorialized that he should not again serve as a palace official.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices, citing the criminal offense of Shu's father's younger cousin, memorialized that he should not again serve as a palace official.

sentences.zh: 璹上言：「昔王敦稱兵犯順，王導仍典樞機；

translations.literal: Shu submitted, saying: "Formerly when Wang Dun raised troops in rebellion, Wang Dao still held the keys of state;
translations.idiomatic: Shu submitted a memorial: "In the past, when Wang Dun raised troops in rebellion, Wang Dao still held the keys of state;

sentences.zh: 嵇康戮於晉朝，嵇紹忠於晉室。

translations.literal: Ji Kang was executed in the Jin dynasty, yet Ji Shao remained loyal to the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang was put to death under the Jin, yet Ji Shao remained loyal to the Jin house.

sentences.zh: 竊惟前古，尚不爲疑；

translations.literal: Privately considering antiquity, still they were not held in doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on antiquity, such cases aroused no suspicion;

sentences.zh: 今奉聖恩，豈由臣下。

translations.literal: Now receiving the sacred grace, how could it be owing to subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I receive Your Majesty's grace, how could this depend on a subordinate's merit?

sentences.zh: 必以體例有乖，伏請甘從屏退。」

translations.literal: If it must be because the regulations are at variance, I humbly request willingly to submit to dismissal."
translations.idiomatic: If the regulations truly forbid it, I humbly ask to accept removal from office."

sentences.zh: 則天曰：「此乃我意，卿復何言！

translations.literal: Wu Zetian said: "This is my intent—what more have you to say!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian said: "This is my decision—what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 但當盡忠，無聽浮説。」

translations.literal: You need only devote loyalty; do not heed loose talk."
translations.idiomatic: Simply remain loyal, and pay no heed to idle talk."

sentences.zh: 時武三思率蕃夷酋長，請造天樞於端門外，刻字紀功，以頌周德，璹爲督作使。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sansi led tribal chiefs of frontier peoples, requesting to build the Celestial Axis outside the Duan Gate, inscribing characters to record merit and praise Zhou virtue; Shu served as superintendent of construction.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Sansi led tribal chiefs from the frontier in requesting that the Celestial Axis be erected outside the Duan Gate, with inscriptions recording merit to praise the virtue of Zhou; Shu was made superintendent of the project.

sentences.zh: 證聖初，璹加秋官尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengsheng, Shu was additionally made Minister of Autumn and Co-equal Chief Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengsheng era, Shu was further appointed Minister of the Autumn Office and Co-Chief Counselor.

sentences.zh: 是歳，明堂災，則天欲責躬避正殿，璹奏曰：「此實人火，非曰天災。

translations.literal: That year the Bright Hall suffered disaster; Wu Zetian wished to blame herself and avoid the main hall. Shu memorialized: "This is truly human fire, not what is called a heaven-sent calamity.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Bright Hall burned; Wu Zetian wished to accept blame and withdraw from the main hall. Shu submitted: "This was plainly human fire, not a heaven-sent disaster.

sentences.zh: 至如成周宣榭，卜代愈隆；

translations.literal: As for the Xuan tower of completed Zhou, divining the succession it grew ever more lofty;
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Xuan tower of the Zhou: though it burned, divination showed the dynasty would grow ever greater;

sentences.zh: 漢武建章，盛德彌永。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han's Jianzhang Palace—splendid virtue ever more enduring.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's Jianzhang Palace likewise rose again, and his great virtue endured all the longer.

sentences.zh: 臣又見《彌勒下生經》雲，當彌勒成佛之時，七寶臺須臾散壞。

translations.literal: Your subject has also seen the Scripture of Maitreya's Descent, which says: when Maitreya becomes Buddha, the seven-jewel platform in an instant scatters and breaks.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also read in the Scripture of Maitreya's Descent that when Maitreya attains Buddhahood, the seven-jewel platform momentarily crumbles and falls.

sentences.zh: 睹此無常之相，便成正覺之因。

translations.literal: Perceiving this sign of impermanence, one then completes the cause of true awakening.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this mark of impermanence becomes the very cause of true enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 故知聖人之道，隨緣示化，方便之利，博濟良多。

translations.literal: Thus one knows the way of sages—following conditions to manifest transformation; the benefit of expedient means broadly aids many.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that the sage's way adapts to conditions to teach, and that skillful means can bring vast benefit to many.

sentences.zh: 可使由之，義存於此。

translations.literal: That one may be led to follow it—the principle lies herein.
translations.idiomatic: The principle that rulers may continue their course despite such events is precisely here.

sentences.zh: 況今明堂，乃是布政之所，非宗廟之地，陛下若避正殿，於禮未爲得也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the present Bright Hall is the place for administering government, not the site of the ancestral temple; if Your Majesty avoids the main hall, in ritual it is not quite fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Bright Hall is where government is conducted, not the ancestral shrine. For Your Majesty to withdraw from the main hall would not accord with ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 左拾遺劉承慶廷奏云：「明堂宗祀之所，今既被焚，陛下宜輟朝思過。」

translations.literal: The Left Reminder Liu Chengqing memorialized at court: "The Bright Hall is the place of ancestral sacrifice; now that it has been burned, Your Majesty should suspend court and reflect on faults."
translations.idiomatic: The Left Reminder Liu Chengqing argued at court: "The Bright Hall is where the ruler sacrifices to ancestors. Now that it has burned, Your Majesty should suspend court and reflect on your conduct."

sentences.zh: 璹又持前議以爭之，則天乃依璹奏。

translations.literal: Shu again held to his earlier proposal and disputed it; Wu Zetian then followed Shu's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shu again pressed his earlier argument, and Wu Zetian sided with his memorial.

sentences.zh: 先令璹監造天樞，至是以功當賜爵一等。

translations.literal: Previously Shu had been ordered to supervise construction of the Celestial Axis; now by merit he was due to be granted one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had earlier been charged with supervising the Celestial Axis, and for this service he was now granted one step in rank of nobility.

sentences.zh: 璹表請回贈父一官，乃追贈其父豫州司戸參軍處平爲博州刺史。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized requesting to turn back and enfeoff his father with one office; thereupon his father Chuping, Administrative Assistant of the Prefecture Office of Yuzhou, was posthumously enfeoffed as Prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shu asked that the reward be applied instead to posthumous honors for his father; his father Chuping, formerly Administrative Assistant of the Yuzhou Prefecture Office, was then posthumously given the title Prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 天後將封嵩嶽，命璹總知撰儀注，並充封禪副使。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress was about to perform the fengshan on Mount Song; she ordered Shu to take general charge of composing the ritual protocols and also to serve as deputy commissioner for fengshan.
translations.idiomatic: As the Heavenly Empress prepared to perform the fengshan rite at Mount Song, she put Shu in charge of drafting the ritual protocols and appointed him deputy commissioner of the rite.

sentences.zh: 及重造明堂，又令璹充使督作，以功加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was rebuilt, she again ordered Shu to serve as commissioner supervising construction; by merit he was given the title Silver Azure Glory Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall was rebuilt, she again appointed Shu to supervise the work, and for this service he was granted the title Silver Azure Glory Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 時有大石國使請獻獅子，璹上疏諫曰：「獅子猛獸，唯止食肉，遠從碎葉，以至神都，肉既難得，檢爲勞費。

translations.literal: At the time an envoy of the Kingdom of Da Shi requested to present a lion. Shu submitted a remonstrance: "Lions are ferocious beasts that eat only meat; coming from afar from Suyab to reach the Divine Capital, meat is hard to obtain, and guarding it becomes labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy from the Kingdom of Da Shi asked to present a lion. Shu remonstrated: "The lion is a fierce beast that eats only meat. Brought from distant Suyab all the way to the Divine Capital, meat would be hard to supply, and keeping it would mean endless labor and expense.

sentences.zh: 陛下以百姓爲心，慮一物有失，鷹犬不蓄，漁獵總停。

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes the common people as your heart, fearing any creature should suffer loss; hawks and dogs are not kept, fishing and hunting are entirely stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heart is with the people, and you shrink from any harm to living things: you keep no hawks or dogs and have banned all fishing and hunting.

sentences.zh: 運不殺以闡大慈，垂好生以敷至德，凡在飛蠢動，莫不感荷仁恩。

translations.literal: Upholding non-killing to unfold great compassion, extending love of life to spread supreme virtue—all that fly or crawl feel and bear your benevolent grace.
translations.idiomatic: You uphold non-killing to spread great compassion and cherish life to manifest supreme virtue; every creature that flies or crawls has felt your kindness.

sentences.zh: 豈容自菲薄於身，而厚資給於獸，求之至理，必不然乎。」

translations.literal: How could it be fitting to be sparing toward yourself yet lavishly supply beasts? Seeking the utmost principle, surely it cannot be so."
translations.idiomatic: How can you be frugal toward yourself yet lavish in maintaining a beast? By any sound principle, this cannot be right."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，遽停來使。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, and the incoming envoy was immediately stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and the envoy's visit was promptly canceled.

sentences.zh: 又九鼎初成，製令黃金千兩塗之。

translations.literal: Again, when the Nine Cauldrons were first completed, an edict ordered them gilded with a thousand taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nine Cauldrons were first completed, an edict ordered them plated with a thousand taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 璹進諫曰：「夫鼎者神器，貴在質樸自然，無假別爲浮飾。

translations.literal: Shu submitted remonstrance: "Cauldrons are sacred vessels; what is valued is plain simplicity and naturalness—there is no need to add separate ornate decoration.
translations.idiomatic: Shu remonstrated: "Cauldrons are sacred vessels. Their value lies in plain, natural simplicity; they need no added ornament.

sentences.zh: 臣觀其狀，先有五彩輝煥，錯雜其間，豈待金色，方爲炫耀？」

translations.literal: Your subject observes their form: already there is five-colored brilliance flashing, intermingled among them—must one wait for gold before they become dazzling?"
translations.idiomatic: I see that they already shine with five colors interwoven among them—must they be gilded before they can dazzle?"

sentences.zh: 則天又從之。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian again accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 尋屬契丹犯塞，命梁王武三思爲榆關道安撫大使、璹爲副使以備之。

translations.literal: Soon the Khitans violated the frontier; Prince of Liang Wu Sansi was ordered as Pacification Commissioner of the Yuguan Circuit, and Shu as deputy commissioner to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Khitans raided the frontier. Prince Wu Sansi of Liang was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Yuguan Circuit, with Shu as deputy, to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 及還，坐事，神功初左授益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: When they returned, implicated in an offense, at the beginning of Shenggong he was demoted to Left-appointed Chief Secretary of the Great Protectorate of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After their return he was implicated in an offense and, at the beginning of the Shenggong era, was demoted to Chief Secretary of the Yizhou Metropolitan Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 蜀中官吏多貪暴，璹屢有發擿，奸無所容。

translations.literal: Officials in Shu were mostly greedy and violent; Shu repeatedly exposed cases, and wrongdoing had no refuge.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in Shu were notoriously greedy and brutal, but Shu repeatedly exposed their crimes until wrongdoing had no place to hide.

sentences.zh: 則天嘉之，降璽書勞之曰：「夫嚴霜之下，識貞鬆之擅奇，疾風之前，知勁草之爲貴。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian praised this and sent down an imperial letter commending him: "Under harsh frost one recognizes the pine's singular firmness; before fierce wind one knows the tough grass's worth.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian was pleased and sent an imperial letter of commendation: "Under hard frost one learns how singular the pine's constancy is; in a sharp wind one sees how precious tough grass can be.

sentences.zh: 物既有此，人亦宜哉。

translations.literal: If things have this, people too should be so.
translations.idiomatic: If even plants show such qualities, how much more should men.

sentences.zh: 卿早荷朝恩，委任斯重。

translations.literal: You early received the court's grace; the trust placed in you is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: You have long enjoyed the court's favor and been entrusted with weighty responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 居中作相，弘益已多，防邊訓兵，心力俱盡。

translations.literal: Serving at center as chief counselor, your broad benefits have already been many; guarding the frontier and training troops, heart and strength both exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: As chief counselor at court you have already brought great benefit; guarding the frontier and drilling troops, you have given your utmost in body and mind.

sentences.zh: 歳寒無改，終始不渝。

translations.literal: In cold year's end no change—beginning to end without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Unchanged through the year's cold, steadfast from first to last.

sentences.zh: 乃眷蜀中，氓俗殷雜，久缺良守，弊於侵漁，政以賄成，人無措足。

translations.literal: Turning regard to Shu: its people and customs are numerous and mixed; long lacking good governors, afflicted by predation; government achieved through bribes, people without place to set foot.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Shu: its people are numerous, its customs complex, and good governors have long been lacking. Predatory officials have made government a matter of bribes, and the people can scarcely find footing.

sentences.zh: 是用命卿出鎮，寄茲存養。

translations.literal: Therefore I ordered you to go out and garrison there, entrusting to you their preservation and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason I sent you to govern there, trusting you to preserve and nurture the people.

sentences.zh: 果能攬轡澄清，下車整肅。

translations.literal: Truly able to take the reins and clarify, upon dismounting from the carriage you brought order.
translations.idiomatic: You have indeed taken office like a rider reining in a fouled stream, and from the day you arrived you brought order.

sentences.zh: 吏不敢犯，奸無所容，前後糾擿，蓋非一緒。

translations.literal: Officials dare not offend, wrongdoing has no refuge; rectifications before and after cover not merely one category.
translations.idiomatic: Officials dare not transgress, and wrongdoers have nowhere to hide; your repeated investigations have not been few.

sentences.zh: 貪殘之伍，屏跡於列城；

translations.literal: The band of greedy and cruel flee from sight in the walled cities;
translations.idiomatic: The greedy and brutal have vanished from the cities;

sentences.zh: 剽奪之儔，遁形於外境。

translations.literal: The company of pillagers hide their forms beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: plunderers have fled beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 詎勞期月，康此黎元，言念德聲，良深嘉尚。

translations.literal: Needing hardly a month's labor, you have brought peace to these common people; speaking of your virtuous repute, I deeply commend and esteem it.
translations.idiomatic: In hardly a month you have brought ease to the people. At the thought of your virtuous reputation, I am deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 宜布琅邪之化，當以豫州爲法。」
