translations.literal: You should spread the governance of Langye; take Yuzhou as the model."
translations.idiomatic: Continue to spread the governance you showed at Langye, and let Yuzhou be your model."

sentences.zh: 則天又嘗謂侍臣曰：「凡爲長官，能清自身者甚易，清得僚吏者甚難。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian also once told attendant ministers: "For anyone holding chief office, making oneself pure is very easy; making subordinate officials pure is very hard.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian also once told her ministers: "For any chief official, keeping oneself clean is easy; keeping one's subordinates clean is hard.

sentences.zh: 至於姚璹，可謂兼之矣。」

translations.literal: As for Yao Shu, one may say he has achieved both."
translations.idiomatic: As for Yao Shu, one may say he has done both."

sentences.zh: 時新都丞朱待辟坐贓至死，逮捕繫獄。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Daibi, Assistant Prefect of Xindu, was implicated in embezzlement and sentenced to death; he was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Daibi, assistant prefect of Xindu, was convicted of embezzlement and sentenced to death; he was arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 待辟素善沙門理中，陰結諸不逞，因待辟以殺璹爲名，擬據巴蜀爲亂。

translations.literal: Daibi had long been close to the monk Lizhong, secretly joined with various malcontents, and using Daibi's case took killing Shu as their rallying cry, planning to seize Bashu and raise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Daibi had long been close to the monk Lizhong and secretly united malcontents. Using his case as pretext, they plotted to kill Shu, seize Bashu, and rebel.

sentences.zh: 人密表告之者，製令璹按其獄。

translations.literal: Someone secretly memorialized to inform on this; an edict ordered Shu to investigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: When someone secretly reported the plot, an edict put Shu in charge of the investigation.

sentences.zh: 璹深持之，事涉疑似引而誅死者，僅以千數。

translations.literal: Shu pursued it deeply; matters touching suspicion led to executions numbering nearly a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pressed the case relentlessly, and where suspicion touched, executions ran to nearly a thousand.

sentences.zh: 則天又令洛州長史宋元爽、御史中丞霍獻可等重加詳覆，亦無所發明。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian again ordered Chief Secretary of Luozhou Song Yuanshuang, Vice Censor-in-Chief Huo Xiank, and others to review again in detail, yet they also found nothing newly brought to light.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian also ordered Song Yuanshuang, chief secretary of Luozhou, Vice Censor-in-Chief Huo Xiank, and others to reinvestigate thoroughly, but they too found nothing substantial.

sentences.zh: 逮繫獄數百人，不勝酷毒，遞相附會，以就反狀。

translations.literal: By then several hundred imprisoned could not bear cruel torture; one after another they attached themselves to the story to fit the shape of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: By then several hundred prisoners, unable to endure torture, corroborated one another's confessions until a full case of treason was made.

sentences.zh: 因此籍沒者復五十餘家，其餘稱知反配流者亦十八九，道路冤之。

translations.literal: For this reason more than fifty households again had property confiscated; the rest who claimed knowledge of rebellion were exiled, also eight or nine tenths; people on the roads lamented the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty families were again stripped of property, and eight or nine out of ten others were exiled for allegedly knowing of the plot; people everywhere lamented the injustice.

sentences.zh: 監察御史袁恕己劾奏其事。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Yuan Shuji impeached and memorialized on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising censor Yuan Shuji impeached Shu over the affair.

sentences.zh: 則天初令璹與恕己對定，又尋令罷推。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian at first ordered Shu and Shuji to confront and settle the matter, then soon ordered the investigation stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian first ordered Shu and Shuji to settle the matter face to face, but soon halted the investigation.

sentences.zh: 俄拜地官尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of the Earth Office.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，轉冬官尚書，仍西京留守。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he transferred to Minister of Winter, still serving as Western Capital Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: After a year or more he became Minister of the Winter Office while remaining Garrison Commander of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 長安中，累表乞骸骨，製聽致仕，進爵爲伯。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he repeatedly memorialized requesting to retire; an edict permitted him to leave office, and his nobility was raised to Count.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he repeatedly asked to retire; an edict granted his request, and he was advanced in rank to Count.

sentences.zh: 遇官名復舊，爲工部尚書。

translations.literal: When office titles were restored to the old forms, he became Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When official titles were restored to their old forms, he became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年卒，遺令薄葬，贈越州都督，諡曰成。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong he died; his final instruction was for a plain burial; posthumously given Grand Defender of Yuezhou; posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Shenlong, leaving orders for a plain burial. He was posthumously made Grand Defender of Yuezhou and given the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 璹弟 珽弟珽，少好學，以勤苦自立。

translations.literal: Shu's younger brother Ting—Ting, in youth loved learning and through diligence and hardship stood on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's younger brother Ting loved learning from youth and through tireless effort made his own way.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，累除定、汴、滄、虢、豳等五州刺史，加銀青光祿大夫，轉秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Having passed the Mingjing examination, he was successively appointed Prefect of the five prefectures Ding, Bian, Cang, Guo, and Bin; given the title Silver Azure Glory Grand Master; transferred to Prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the Mingjing examination, he served successively as prefect of Ding, Bian, Cang, Guo, and Bin, was granted the title Silver Azure Glory Grand Master, and was later transferred to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 以善政有聞，璽書褒美，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Renowned for good governance, an imperial letter praised him and granted a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: His good governance won renown, and he received an imperial letter of praise together with a gift of a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，累封宣城郡公，三遷太子詹事，仍兼左庶子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng Commandery; thrice promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, still concurrently Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong he was ennobled Duke of Xuancheng Commandery, was thrice promoted until he reached Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and concurrently served as Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時節湣太子舉事不法，班前後上書進諫。

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Jiemin acted unlawfully in his affairs; Ting before and after submitted memorials remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Crown Prince Jiemin behaved lawlessly, and Ting repeatedly submitted memorials of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 今載四事：

translations.literal: Now four matters are recorded:
translations.idiomatic: Four of his remonstrances are recorded here:

sentences.zh: 其一曰：臣聞賈誼曰：「選天下之端士，孝悌博聞有道術者，使與太子居處出入。

translations.literal: The first says: Your subject has heard Jia Yi say: "Select the most upright men in the realm, those filial, fraternal, broadly learned and possessing the Way and skill, and have them dwell and go in and out with the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The first reads: I have heard Jia Yi say: 'Choose the most upright men in the empire—those known for filial piety and fraternity, broad learning, and mastery of the Way—and let them live with the Heir Apparent, sharing his daily comings and goings.

sentences.zh: 故太子見正事，聞正言，行正道，左右前後皆正人也。

translations.literal: Thus the Heir Apparent sees upright affairs, hears upright words, walks the upright path—left, right, before, and behind are all upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Heir Apparent will see what is right, hear what is right, and do what is right, with upright men on every side.

sentences.zh: 夫習與正人居之，不能無正；

translations.literal: For habituated to dwell with upright men, one cannot but be upright;
translations.idiomatic: For one who keeps company with upright men cannot fail to become upright;

sentences.zh: 習與不正人居之，不能無不正。

translations.literal: Habituated to dwell with un upright men, one cannot but be un upright.
translations.idiomatic: and one who keeps company with the un upright cannot fail to become un upright.

sentences.zh: 太子既冠成人，免於保傅之嚴，則有記過之史。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent has capped adulthood, released from tutors' strictness, then there are historians who record faults.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent comes of age and is freed from the tutors' strict oversight, historians record his faults,

sentences.zh: 徹膳之宰，進善之旌，誹謗之木，敢諫之鼓，瞽史誦箴，大夫進謀，故習與智長，化與心成。

translations.literal: Stewards who withdraw meals, banners for advancing good, the slander wood, the drum for bold remonstrance, blind historians reciting admonitions, grandees advancing counsel—thus habit grows with wisdom, transformation completes with the heart.
translations.idiomatic: stewards who withhold meals, banners for promoting good conduct, the wooden post for criticism, the drum for bold remonstrance, blind historians reciting admonitions, and grand officers offering counsel—thus habit grows into wisdom and transformation becomes second nature.

sentences.zh: 夫教得而左右正，則太子正矣；

translations.literal: When teaching succeeds and those at left and right are upright, then the Heir Apparent is upright;
translations.idiomatic: When instruction succeeds and those around him are upright, the Heir Apparent becomes upright;

sentences.zh: 太子正而天下定矣。」

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent is upright, the realm is settled."
translations.idiomatic: when the Heir Apparent is upright, the realm is secure.'

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之，木從繩則正，後從諫則聖。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard: wood following the line becomes straight; a ruler following remonstrance becomes sage.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that wood straightened to the line becomes true, and a ruler who heeds remonstrance becomes a sage.

sentences.zh: 善言古者，所以驗於今。

translations.literal: Good words about antiquity are means to test against the present.
translations.idiomatic: Fine words about the past are meant to test the present.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下睿德洪深，天姿聰敏，近代成敗，前古安危，莫不懸鑒在心，動合典禮。

translations.literal: Humbly reflecting: Your Highness's sage virtue is vast and deep, Heaven-endowed wit keen and sharp; recent successes and failures, ancient security and danger—all hang as mirrors in the heart, actions matching canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's wisdom runs deep and your native wit is keen. Recent successes and failures, ancient triumphs and catastrophes—all hang before you like mirrors, and your every act accords with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸朽，濫居輔弼，虛備耳目，叨預股肱，輒薦塵露，庶裨山海。

translations.literal: Your subject, withered and worthless, rashly occupies a supporting post; vainly filling the role of eyes and ears, presumptuously among arms and legs—rashly offering dust and dew, hoping it may aid mountains and seas.
translations.idiomatic: I am old and worthless, unworthy of my post as counselor, yet I serve as Your Highness's eyes and ears and bear, however unworthily, a share in your trust. I venture to offer this trifling counsel in hope it may prove of some use.

sentences.zh: 伏以內置作坊，工巧得入宮闈之內、禁衞之所，或言語內出，或事狀外通，小人無知，不識輕重，因爲詐偽，有玷徽猷。

translations.literal: Humbly reflecting: workshops established within the palace—artisans may enter the inner quarters and forbidden guard precincts; sometimes speech goes out from within, sometimes affairs reach outside—petty men ignorant, not knowing weight and light, thereby commit fraud, tarnishing fine governance.
translations.idiomatic: Workshops inside the palace allow craftsmen into the inner quarters and guarded precincts. Matters are sometimes discussed inside and sometimes communicated outside; ignorant petty men, failing to grasp what is at stake, may commit fraud and bring disgrace upon your reputation for fine governance.

sentences.zh: 臣望並付所司，以停宮內造作。

translations.literal: Your subject hopes all will be entrusted to the responsible offices, stopping construction within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these workshops be placed under the proper offices and all palace construction halted.

sentences.zh: 如或要須役造，猶望宮外安置，庶得工匠不於宮禁出入。

translations.literal: If labor and construction are truly necessary, still hoping for placement outside the palace, so that artisans need not go in and out of the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: If any work is truly needed, let it be set up outside the palace so craftsmen need not enter and leave the forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：臣聞漢文帝身衣弋綈，足履革舄；

translations.literal: The second says: Your subject has heard Emperor Wen of Han wore coarse silk and leather shoes;
translations.idiomatic: The second reads: I am told that Emperor Wen of the Han wore coarse silk and leather shoes;

sentences.zh: 齊高帝欄檻用銅者，皆易以鐵。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi—wherever railings used copper, all were replaced with iron.
translations.idiomatic: and Emperor Gao of Qi replaced every copper railing with iron.

sentences.zh: 經侯帶玉具劍環珮以過魏，太子不視，經侯曰：「魏國亦有寶乎？」

translations.literal: Marquis Jing wore a jade-fitted sword with ring and pendant passing through Wei; the Heir Apparent did not look. Marquis Jing said: "Does the state of Wei also have treasures?"
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis Jing passed through Wei wearing a jade-fitted sword with ring and pendant, the crown prince did not so much as glance at it. Marquis Jing asked: "Does Wei possess treasures of its own?"

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「主信臣忠，魏之寶也。」

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent said: "The ruler's trust and the minister's loyalty—Wei's treasure."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince replied: "The ruler's trust and the minister's loyalty—that is Wei's treasure."

sentences.zh: 經侯委劍珮而去。

translations.literal: Marquis Jing cast aside sword and pendant and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jing laid down his sword and pendant and left.

sentences.zh: 太子使追還之，謂曰：「珠玉珍玩，寒不可衣，饑不可食，無遺我賊。」

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent sent someone to pursue and return them, saying: "Pearls, jade, and rare curios—cold cannot be clothed by them, hunger cannot be fed by them; do not bequeath me thieves."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince sent a man after him to return them, saying: "Pearls, jade, and precious trifles cannot keep one warm in cold or fed in hunger. Do not leave me thieves instead of treasures."

sentences.zh: 經侯杜門不出。

translations.literal: Marquis Jing shut his door and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: After that Marquis Jing shut his door and never went out again.

sentences.zh: 臣觀聖賢經籍，務以簡素爲貴；

translations.literal: Your subject observes that in sage and worthies' classic books, simplicity is prized;
translations.idiomatic: The classics of sages and worthies hold simplicity in highest esteem;

sentences.zh: 皇王政化，皆以菲薄爲德。

translations.literal: Imperial kings' government and transformation all take frugality as virtue.
translations.idiomatic: and the governance of sage rulers takes frugality as virtue.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下留心恭儉，靡尚浮奢。

translations.literal: Humbly reflecting: Your Highness attends to respect and frugality, not cherishing empty extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness already practices reverence and thrift and does not indulge in empty extravagance.

sentences.zh: 臣愚猶望損之又損之，居簡以行簡，減省造作，節量用度。

translations.literal: Your subject in foolishness still hopes to reduce yet further, dwell in simplicity and act in simplicity, reduce construction, economize expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I still venture to hope you will reduce again and again: live simply, act simply, cut construction, and measure every expense.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：臣聞銀牖銅樓，宮闈嚴秘，門閤來往，皆有簿歴。

translations.literal: The third says: Your subject has heard that with silver windows and bronze towers, palace quarters are strictly secret; comings and goings at gates all have ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: The third reads: I understand that the palace quarters, with their silver lattices and bronze towers, are strictly guarded, and every passage through the gates is recorded in ledgers.

sentences.zh: 殿下時有所須，唯門司宣令，或恐奸偽之輩，因此妄爲增減，脫有文狀舛錯，事理便即差違。

translations.literal: When Your Highness sometimes has need, only the gate office announces orders; one fears fraudulent persons thereby recklessly adding or subtracting; if documents are mistaken, affairs and principle at once diverge.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Highness requires something, the gate office alone proclaims the order. I fear that frauds may exploit this to alter commands at will; should any document be wrong, the result would immediately go astray.

sentences.zh: 且近日呂升之便乃代署宣敕，伏賴殿下睿敏，當即覺其奸偽，自餘臣下庸淺，豈能深辨真虛？

translations.literal: Moreover, recently Lü Shengzhi presumptuously substituted signatures on proclaimed edicts; relying humbly on Your Highness's keen wisdom, you instantly perceived the fraud—but remaining subordinates are shallow and base; how could they deeply distinguish true from false?
translations.idiomatic: Only recently Lü Shengzhi dared to sign edicts in others' stead. Thanks to Your Highness's sharp wit, the fraud was caught at once—but other officials are neither so keen nor so vigilant. How could they tell truth from forgery?

sentences.zh: 望墨令及覆事行下，並用內印印畫署之後，冀得免有詐假，乃是長久規模。

translations.literal: I hope that when ink orders and returned matters are issued downward, all may be imprinted with the inner seal and signed afterward, hoping thereby to avoid fraud—it would be a lasting model.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that every written order and every return submitted for action be stamped with the inner seal and signed only after that, so forgeries may be prevented. That would be a permanent safeguard.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之，忠臣事君，有犯而無隱；

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that a loyal minister serving his lord has offense yet no concealment;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that a loyal minister serves his ruler by speaking out rather than hiding his views;

sentences.zh: 明主馭下，納諫以進德。

translations.literal: an enlightened lord controlling his subordinates accepts remonstrance to advance in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: and that a wise sovereign governs his officials by accepting remonstrance to grow in virtue.

sentences.zh: 故《書》云：「有言逆於誌，必求諸道；

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents says: "When words run counter to one's intent, one must seek them in the Way;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "When words go against your wish, examine them by the Way;

sentences.zh: 有言順於心，必求諸非道。」

translations.literal: when words accord with the heart, one must seek them in what is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: when words please your heart, examine them for what is not the Way."

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下仁明昭著，聖敬日躋，探幽洞微，窮神索隱。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Highness's benevolence and clarity are manifest, sacred reverence daily ascends, probing the obscure and penetrating the subtle, exhausting the spirit and seeking the hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is manifestly benevolent and clear-sighted, your sacred reverence grows daily, and you probe the deepest mysteries.

sentences.zh: 事之善惡，毫厘靡差；

translations.literal: In the good or evil of affairs, not a hair's breadth errs;
translations.idiomatic: You judge good and evil in affairs to a hair's breadth;

sentences.zh: 理有危疑，錙銖無爽。

translations.literal: where principle is perilous or doubtful, not a grain's weight misses.
translations.idiomatic: and where principle is doubtful, not the smallest weight escapes you.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸謬，叨侍春闈，職居獻替，豈敢緘默！

translations.literal: Your subject, being mediocre and mistaken, presumptuously attends the spring gate; his office is to offer and replace—how would he dare be silent!
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy to serve in your household, yet my duty is to counsel and correct—how dare I remain silent!

sentences.zh: 其四曰：臣聞聖人不專其德，賢智必有所師。

translations.literal: The fourth point: your subject has heard that the sage does not monopolize his virtue; the worthy and wise must have someone to learn from.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: I have heard that sages do not rely on virtue alone—the worthy and wise must have teachers.

sentences.zh: 故曰：與善人言，如入芝蘭之室，久自芬芳；

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: speaking with a good man is like entering a room of orchids and angelica—after long time one becomes fragrant oneself;
translations.idiomatic: They say that talking with good men is like entering a room of orchids: in time you take on their fragrance;

sentences.zh: 與不善人言，如火銷膏，不覺而盡。

translations.literal: speaking with a bad man is like fire melting grease—before one knows it, all is gone.
translations.idiomatic: talking with bad men is like fire melting fat—you are consumed before you know it.

sentences.zh: 今司經見無學士，供奉未有侍讀，伏望時因視膳，奏請置人。

translations.literal: Now the Directorate of Classics has no erudite scholars, and the Palace Service has no lecturing attendants. I humbly hope that when Your Highness attends to your parents' meals, you may memorialize to appoint such men.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Directorate of Classics lacks learned scholars, and the palace staff has no reading tutors. I beg that when you attend your parents at meals, you ask to have such men appointed.

sentences.zh: 所冀講席談筵，務盡忠規之道；

translations.literal: What is hoped is that at lecture seats and discussion mats, the way of loyal counsel may be fully pursued;
translations.idiomatic: Then at lecture and discussion you may fully pursue loyal counsel;

sentences.zh: 披文擿句，方資審諭之勤。

translations.literal: unfolding texts and plucking phrases will then supply the diligence of careful instruction.
translations.idiomatic: and by unfolding texts and weighing phrases you will gain the benefit of careful instruction.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞臣之事主，必盡乃誠；

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that a minister serving his lord must exhaust his sincerity;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that a minister must serve his lord with full sincerity;

sentences.zh: 君之進賢，務求忠讜。

translations.literal: a lord's advancement of the worthy must seek loyal and forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: and a ruler who promotes the worthy must seek loyal and forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下養德儲闈，以端靜爲務；

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Highness, nurturing virtue in the Eastern Palace, should make dignity and quiet your task;
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is cultivating virtue in the Eastern Palace and should make dignity and restraint your aim;

sentences.zh: 恭膺守器，以學業爲先。

translations.literal: reverently bearing the vessel to be guarded, you should put study first.
translations.idiomatic: as heir you should put learning first.

sentences.zh: 經所以立行修身，史所以諳識成敗。

translations.literal: The classics are for establishing conduct and cultivating the person; histories are for becoming versed in success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: The classics teach how to live and cultivate the self; histories teach how to know success and failure.

sentences.zh: 雅誥既習，忠孝乃成，傳記方通，安危斯辨。

translations.literal: When elegant pronouncements are mastered, loyalty and filial piety are achieved; when chronicles and biographies are understood, safety and peril are distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Master the classics and loyalty and filial piety follow; master the histories and you can tell safety from peril.

sentences.zh: 知父子君臣之道，識古今鑒戒之規，經史爲先，斯乃急務。

translations.literal: Knowing the way of father and son, ruler and minister, recognizing the rules of ancient and modern mirrors and warnings—classics and histories first: this is the urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: To know the duties of father and son, ruler and subject, and the lessons of past and present—classics and histories must come first; that is the urgent task.

sentences.zh: 至於工巧造作，僚吏直司，實爲末事，無足勞慮。

translations.literal: As for craftsmanship and construction, clerks and direct offices—these are truly minor matters, not worth troubling over.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmanship and construction, the business of clerks and artisans, are truly minor matters not worth your concern.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸淺，獻替是司，臣而不言，負譴聖日，言而獲罪，是所甘心。

translations.literal: Your subject, being mediocre and shallow, is charged with offering and replacing; if as minister he does not speak, he bears reproach on a sacred day; if he speaks and receives punishment, that is what his heart accepts.
translations.idiomatic: I am shallow and unworthy, yet my office is to counsel; if I do not speak I fail my duty, and if speaking brings punishment I accept it willingly.

sentences.zh: 伏願留意經書，簡略細事，一蒙采納，萬殞無辭。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will attend to the classics and set aside minor affairs; if once accepted, though I die ten thousand deaths I will have no complaint.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to heed the classics and set minor affairs aside; if you accept this counsel once, I would die ten thousand deaths without regret.

sentences.zh: 乞降儲明，俯矜狂瞽。

translations.literal: I beg you to lower your stored brilliance and look down with pity on this mad blindness.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to lend your wisdom and pity this rash blindness.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，太子雖稱善，竟不悛革。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Crown Prince though he praised it did not in the end reform.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Crown Prince praised it but did not reform.

sentences.zh: 太子敗，詔遣索其宮中，得班諫書，中宗嘉其切直。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was defeated, an edict was sent to search his palace quarters; Ban's remonstrance writings were found, and Emperor Zhongzong praised their blunt directness.
translations.idiomatic: After the Crown Prince's fall, an edict searched his quarters and found Ban's remonstrances; Emperor Zhongzong praised their blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 時宮臣皆貶黜，唯班擢拜右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the time all palace officials were demoted; only Ban was promoted and appointed Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: While other palace officials were demoted, Ban alone was promoted to Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，累授戸部尚書，轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he was repeatedly appointed Minister of Revenue and transferred to Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong came to the throne, Ban was appointed Minister of Revenue and later Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，加金紫光祿大夫，復拜戸部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian he was given the honorary title Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Bright Light and again appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantian 2 (713) he was made Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Bright Light and again appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 班與兄弟璹，數年間俱爲定州刺史、戸部尚書，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Ban and his brother Shuo within several years were both Prefect of Dingzhou and Minister of Revenue; people of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: Ban and his brother Shuo both served as prefect of Dingzhou and Minister of Revenue within a few years—a distinction people envied.

sentences.zh: 開元二年卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Kaiyuan, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kaiyuan 2 (714) at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 班嘗以其曾祖察所撰《漢書訓纂》，多爲後之注《漢書》者隱沒名氏，將爲己説；

translations.literal: Ban once noted that the Han shu Exegetical Compendium compiled by his great-grandfather Cha was often used by later commentators on the Han shu, who concealed the author's name and treated it as their own doctrine;
translations.idiomatic: Ban observed that his great-grandfather Cha's Exegetical Compendium of the Han History was often used by later Han shu commentators, who hid Cha's name and passed the work off as their own;

sentences.zh: 班乃撰《漢書紹訓》四十卷，以發明舊義，行於代。

translations.literal: Ban therefore compiled forty scrolls of Continuation of the Han shu Exegesis to clarify the old meanings, and it circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: so Ban compiled forty scrolls of Continuation of the Han Exegesis to restore the original meaning, and it circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：天子有諍臣七人，雖無道不失其天下。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: A Son of Heaven has seven remonstrating ministers; though he be without the Way he does not lose his realm.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: A Son of Heaven has seven remonstrating ministers; even if he lacks the Way he will not lose the realm.

sentences.zh: 致廬陵復位，唐祚中興，諍由狄公，一人以蔽。

translations.literal: Bringing back the Lord of Luling to restoration, the Tang fortune was revived—remonstrance came from Lord Di; one man suffices to cover the case.
translations.idiomatic: Restoring the Lord of Luling and reviving the Tang house came through remonstrance—and Lord Di alone is enough to prove the point.

sentences.zh: 或曰：許之太甚。

translations.literal: Someone said: This praises him too much.
translations.idiomatic: Some say this praises him excessively.

sentences.zh: 答曰：當革命之時，朋邪甚眾，非推誠竭力，致身忘家者，孰能與於此乎！

translations.literal: The answer was: In a time of dynastic transformation, factional evil was very numerous; unless one pushed sincerity to the utmost, gave his body and forgot his family, who could share in this!
translations.idiomatic: The reply: In a time of revolution, wicked factions were everywhere—who but a man who gave his whole heart, body, and family could have done what he did?

sentences.zh: 仁傑流死不避，骨鯁有彰，雖逢好殺無辜，能使終畏大義。

translations.literal: Renjie did not avoid exile and death; his backbone was manifest. Though he met a ruler who loved killing the innocent, he could make her in the end fear great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie faced exile and death without flinching, and his integrity was plain. Though he served a ruler who killed freely, he made her fear the claims of justice in the end.

sentences.zh: 竟存天下，豈不然乎！

translations.literal: In the end he preserved the realm—is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: He preserved the empire in the end—is that not so?

sentences.zh: 王方慶幹城南海，羽冀東宮，臺閣樞機，無不功濟，所謂君子不器者也。

translations.literal: Wang Fangqing was a shield-wall for the south seas and wings for the Eastern Palace; at the terrace, pavilion, and pivot of state, nothing was without achievement—what is called a gentleman who is not a vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fangqing was a bulwark in the south and a support to the Eastern Palace; in court and in power he succeeded everywhere—a true gentleman of many parts.

sentences.zh: 苟非文學，斯焉取斯。

translations.literal: If not for literary learning, where would he take this from?
translations.idiomatic: Without learning, what would he have had to draw on?

sentences.zh: 璹成都布政，始卒不侔；

translations.literal: Shuo governed Chengdu and spread policy, but beginning and end did not match;
translations.idiomatic: Shuo governed Chengdu well at first but not at the end;

sentences.zh: 相國上章，或否或中。

translations.literal: the chief minister's memorials were sometimes wrong, sometimes right.
translations.idiomatic: the chief minister's memorials were sometimes wrong and sometimes right.

sentences.zh: 且焚明堂而避正殿，固諍何多；

translations.literal: Moreover, burning the Bright Hall and avoiding the main hall—how many firm remonstrances;
translations.idiomatic: He burned the Bright Hall and avoided the main hall—how many bold remonstrances;

sentences.zh: 黜唐頌而立天樞，一言非措。

translations.literal: dismissing Tang hymns and establishing the Heavenly Pivot—one word was not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: yet in dismissing Tang hymns and raising the Heavenly Pivot, one word missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 矧乃妄求符瑞，已失忠貞；

translations.literal: How much more when he rashly sought omens and portents—he had already lost loyal steadfastness;
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, he rashly sought portents and had already lost loyal steadfastness;

sentences.zh: 精擇楚茅，難裨過咎。

translations.literal: carefully selecting Chu thatch could hardly remedy his faults.
translations.idiomatic: carefully choosing Chu thatch could not repair his errors.

sentences.zh: 不常其德，罔畏承羞。

translations.literal: Not constant in his virtue, he did not fear bearing shame.
translations.idiomatic: Inconstant in virtue, he did not fear the shame that follows.

sentences.zh: 班規諫有才，牧守多善，儲幄之任，可謂得人。

translations.literal: Ban had talent in remonstrance and regulation; as prefect and defender he was often good; in the duty of the stored curtain, one may say the right man was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Ban had a gift for remonstrance; as regional governor he did well; in the heir's household he was the right man for the post.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：犯顏忤旨，返政扶危。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Offending the countenance and defying the decree, he restored government and supported peril.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: He offended his ruler's face and defied imperial will, yet restored the dynasty and steadied a crisis.

sentences.zh: 是人雜事，狄能有之。

translations.literal: Among men and mixed affairs, only Di could have this.
translations.idiomatic: Among all men and all affairs, only Di Renjie could do this.

sentences.zh: 終替武氏，克復唐基。

translations.literal: In the end he replaced the Wu clan and recovered the Tang foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He ended the Wu regime and restored the Tang foundation.

sentences.zh: 功之莫大，人無以師。

translations.literal: Of achievements none was greater; among men there is none to take as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: No achievement was greater; no man can be his equal.

sentences.zh: 方慶之才，周旋特立。

translations.literal: Fangqing's talent moved in circles and stood alone.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing's talent was versatile and distinctive.

sentences.zh: 璹也無常，珽能操執。

translations.literal: Shuo was inconstant; Ting could hold fast to principle.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was inconstant; Ting could hold firm to principle.
